title: Misc. bug: RISC-V RVV IQ4_NL/MXFP4 dot product errors with an odd number of blocks due to missing tail handling
body:
### Name and Version

```text
source_commit=b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f
gcc-14 (Bianbu 14.2.0-4ubuntu2~24.04bb2) 14.2.0
Linux k1 6.6.63-cloud #2.2.7.2+20250925145529 SMP PREEMPT Thu Sep 25 10:01:36 UTC 2025 riscv64 riscv64 riscv64 GNU/Linux
```

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Description

The issue is in the RVV implementations in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`. The line references below are based on commit `b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f`.

| Function                         | Loop location                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ggml_vec_dot_iq4_nl_q8_0_vl128` | [L5501-L5532](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L5501-L5532) |
| `ggml_vec_dot_iq4_nl_q8_0_vl256` | [L5556-L5589](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L5556-L5589) |
| `ggml_vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_0_vl128`  | [L6492-L6523](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L6492-L6523) |
| `ggml_vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_0_vl256`  | [L6547-L6580](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c#L6547-L6580) |

These four functions process two quantization blocks per loop iteration. However, there is no tail handling when the number of blocks is odd.

As a result, the final block is skipped and its contribution is not accumulated into the dot-product result, producing an incorrect numerical result.

The behavior is especially clear when `nb = 1`. In that case, the loop condition

```cpp
ib + 1 < nb
```

is false at the initial condition check, so the loop body is never executed and the initially zero-valued `sumf` is returned directly.

I reproduced the issue on a native RISC-V system using a SpacemiT X60 CPU with VLEN=256 and GCC/G++ 14.2.

Codex was used during the initial code analysis and to run the first build and validation workflow on the board over SSH. I subsequently reran the validation programs manually on the same system and confirmed the same results.

On this machine, the directly executed kernels are the `vl256` implementations. The corresponding `vl128` functions have the same two-block loop structure and missing odd-block tail handling, but they were not directly executed on the X60 system used for this reproduction.

The attached reproduction package contains two validation programs:

* a kernel-level differential test comparing the RVV implementation against the generic implementation;
* a `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` test exercising the issue through the actual CPU execution path.

### Related prior work

#8549 fixed a similar odd-block handling issue in earlier `IQ4_NL` CPU implementations. The affected RVV `IQ4_NL` and `MXFP4` kernels were added later in #18859.

The RVV implementations reported here use a two-block loop guarded by `ib + 1 < nb`, so an odd final block is skipped unless it is handled separately. This appears to be an RVV counterpart of the previously identified odd-block handling issue, rather than a duplicate of the same implementation.

## Reproduction

### Environment

The reproduction was tested on:

* native RISC-V Linux;
* SpacemiT X60;
* RVV with measured VLEN = 256 bits;
* an environment supporting the vector and FP16 extensions required by the build, including `Zfh` / `Zvfh`;
* GCC 14.2 / G++ 14.2.

Required tools:

* `gcc-14`
* `g++-14`
* `cmake`
* `ninja`
* `curl`
* `tar`
* `unzip`
* `sha256sum`
* `bash`

The reproduction script invokes `gcc-14` and `g++-14` explicitly, so these command names must be available in `PATH`.

The script does not install dependencies and does not build `llama-cli`.

### Steps

#### 1. Extract the reproduction package

```bash
unzip d1-rvv-reproduction.zip
cd d1-rvv-reproduction
```

#### 2. Download the tested upstream source

The reproduction targets commit:

```text
b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f
```

Download and verify the source archive:

```bash
curl -L --fail -o source.tar.gz \
  https://codeload.github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tar.gz/b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f

printf '%s\n' \
  '6f4183c551303982964148ce591536d3b4ae6e7129085cae640b0c0c20d45982  source.tar.gz' \
  | sha256sum -c -
```

#### 3. Extract the source archive

```bash
tar -xzf source.tar.gz
```

This creates the directory:

```text
llama.cpp-b23701f77d47dad9de834d59ebfcbe25c9e8b46f
```

The reproduction script expects this exact directory name.

#### 4. Build and run the reproduction

```bash
bash run-reproduction.sh
```

The script:

* configures llama.cpp with:

  * `GGML_RVV=ON`
  * `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`
  * `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`
* builds only the required `ggml` / `ggml-cpu` components;
* builds the two validation programs;
* runs both validation programs;
* writes the new logs to `evidence/`;
* records hashes of the relevant source files before execution and checks afterward that those files were not modified during the reproduction.

No model is loaded or executed.

## Expected behavior

All input blocks should contribute to the dot-product computation, regardless of whether the number of blocks is odd or even.

For equivalent inputs, the RVV implementation should therefore agree with the generic implementation within the expected numerical tolerance, and the `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` results should remain correct for odd-block inputs as well.

## Actual result on the affected commit

### Kernel-level differential test

See:

```text
evidence/arch-diff.log
```

On the SpacemiT X60 test system, the log starts with:

```text
vlen_bits=256
```

This value is specific to the test machine; other RISC-V systems should report their actual VLEN.

The test checks 23 quantization types. Differences appear only for `IQ4_NL` and `MXFP4` when the number of blocks is odd.

For `IQ4_NL` and `MXFP4` in this test:

```text
nb = K / 32
```

The mismatches occur at:

```text
nb = 1, 3, 5, 7
```

for both formats, giving eight mismatches in total.

For the single-block case (`nb=1`):

```text
IQ4_NL:
RVV     = 0
generic = -3.514065

MXFP4:
RVV     = 0
generic = 4.612122
```

The final summary is:

```text
types_checked=23 diffs=8
```

### `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` test

See:

```text
evidence/poc-mulmat.log
```

The test contains 21 cases.

`q4_0` passes all tested inputs and is used as a control.

For both `iq4_nl` and `mxfp4`, the following input lengths with odd block counts fail:

```text
K = 32
K = 96
K = 160
K = 224
K = 288
```

The following even-block cases pass:

```text
K = 64
K = 4096
```

Overall:

```text
11 cases passed
10 cases failed
```

The final line is:

```text
total_fail=10
```

This matches the kernel-level failure pattern: only odd-block `IQ4_NL` and `MXFP4` inputs fail.

### Exit status

The reproduction records:

```text
poc_mulmat_exit=1
arch_diff_exit=1
```

Both validation programs intentionally return `1` when they detect numerical mismatches.

The non-zero exit status alone is not sufficient to identify this issue; a successful reproduction should also show the `IQ4_NL` / `MXFP4` odd-block mismatch pattern described above.

`run-reproduction.sh` records the exit status of the validation programs but does not treat their non-zero status as a failure of the wrapper script. Therefore, the wrapper script may still exit with status `0` even when the validation programs return non-zero. The reproduction result should be determined from the recorded logs and the specific mismatch pattern described above.

## Additional notes

`recorded-evidence/` contains logs captured when the reproduction package was prepared. These files are preserved by the reproduction script.

New reproduction logs are written to and overwrite files under:

```text
evidence/
```

The build directory and validation executables may also be regenerated by the script.

After the initial build, the validation programs can be rerun directly:

```bash
./poc_mulmat
echo $?

./arch_diff
echo $?
```

If `codeload.github.com` is inaccessible or unreliable on the target RISC-V system, `source.tar.gz` can be downloaded on another machine and copied into the reproduction directory.

After copying it to the target system, verify the archive using the same `sha256sum` command shown above before extracting it. If the hash check succeeds, continue with:

```bash
tar -xzf source.tar.gz
bash run-reproduction.sh
```

[d1-rvv-reproduction.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32413440/d1-rvv-reproduction.zip)

title: bug: a client-set `X-Conversation-Id` disables disconnect-cancellation and accumulates uncapped resumable-stream sessions, can cause memory DoS
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`. No special launch flag (the resumable-stream manager starts unconditionally at boot).


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 -np 1 --no-webui python3 repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Repro script: [repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/f99b245d040ac2604178c1bef9541d6b#file-repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos-py)

The resumable-stream session manager keys a per-request session on the **client-controlled** `X-Conversation-Id` header. When that header is present, two things go wrong, both exploitable by an unauthenticated client:

**(A) A socket disconnect no longer cancels the generation.** With `X-Conversation-Id`, `server_res_spipe::should_stop()` (`tools/server/server-stream.cpp:622-628`) returns `spipe->is_cancelled()`, which is set only by an explicit `DELETE /v1/stream` — instead of `!conn_alive()`. So a streaming request whose client hangs up keeps the inference slot busy generating to its natural stop. An attacker fires `stream:true` requests with a large `max_tokens` and drops each connection immediately; every abandoned request still consumes a full generation and pins a slot. 

Measured on a single-slot server (`-np 1`): after abandoning one stream, a normal follow-up request was blocked **36.9 s** (the whole generation) with the header, versus **0.07 s** without it (disconnect cancels normally).

**(B) Sessions accumulate with no cap and a 300 s post-completion TTL.** Each session buffers up to `STREAM_SESSION_MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB` of SSE output (`server-stream.cpp:18`) and is retained for `STREAM_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 300 s` **after** the generation completes before the GC removes it (`gc_loop`, `server-stream.cpp:356`). `create_or_replace` (`:235`) just `emplace`s into an `unordered_map,  **there is no cap on the number of sessions**. A client that sends streaming requests with a fresh `X Conversation-Id` each time and never issues `DELETE /v1/stream` accumulates ~`rate × 300 s` sessions, each holding up to 4 MiB, eventually will cause memory exhaustion.

Ablation confirms the header is the cause: 150 streaming requests **without** the header grow `VmHWM` by ~0 MB (sessions are evicted on completion — `on_complete` at `server-stream.cpp:638`), while 150 **with** unique headers retain their sessions (monotonic growth; at large `max_tokens` each retains up to 4 MiB).

title: bug: the GBNF grammar-text parser recurses without a depth limit, can cause stack-overflows and crash server (SIGSEGV)
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 1024 --no-webui python3 repro_llamacpp_gbnf_parser_stackoverflow.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137 --mode paren

# restart, then:
python3 repro_llamacpp_gbnf_parser_stackoverflow.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137 --mode alt
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Repro script: [repro_llamacpp_gbnf_parser_stackoverflow.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/7569b33307bd6c40829f57f337b8c882#file-repro_llamacpp_gbnf_parser_stackoverflow-py)

The GBNF grammar-text parser parses nested groupings with **unbounded mutual recursion**, so a client-supplied `grammar` field with deeply-nested groups (or nested alternations) drives the parser past the stack and **SIGSEGV-kills the whole server**. It is unauthenticated and uncatchable (a stack overflow, not a C++ exception). No special launch flag is needed — the `grammar` field is accepted on `/completion`, `/v1/completions`, and `/v1/chat/completions`.

`llama_grammar_parser::parse_alternates` (`src/llama-grammar.cpp:439`) and `parse_sequence` (`:456`) are mutually recursive: when `parse_sequence` encounters a `(` group it calls `parse_alternates(..., is_nested=true)` at `:602`, which calls `parse_sequence` again. There is no recursion-depth limit, so a grammar such as

```
root ::= (((( … "x" … ))))     # ~100k nested groups
```

recurses ~100k deep and overflows the stack. Confirmed on the CPU build: a valid depth-3 grammar returns `200`, then the depth-100k grammar produces `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` and `/health` stops answering (process dead). Nested alternations `(( … "a"|"b" … ))` crash identically.

### Where it comes from

- `src/llama-grammar.cpp:439` `parse_alternates` → `:445/:449` calls `parse_sequence`.
- `src/llama-grammar.cpp:456` `parse_sequence` → `:602` calls `parse_alternates(..., is_nested=true)` for a `(` group.
- No depth counter bounds the mutual recursion; grammar text length is the only limit.

This is a **different parser and entry point** from the JSON-schema → GBNF converter stack overflow: that one is the `response_format` `json_schema` path in `common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp`; this one is the raw `grammar` field parsed by `src/llama-grammar.cpp`.


**_Happy to provide a fix if requested_**

title: Misc. bug: repeat_last_n / dry_penalty_last_n are not bounded, causing penalties/DRY sampler allocate multi-GB zero-filled buffer and server OOM
body:
### Name and Version

llama-server, git 4b1a27f (version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)), CPU build, Linux x86_64, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
( ulimit -v 5000000; llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 --no-webui ) python3 repro_llamacpp_sampler_penalty_oom.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Repro script:[repro_llamacpp_sampler_penalty_oom.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/17be5c4729c0654d54f7406e6b3bb74b#file-repro_llamacpp_sampler_penalty_oom-py)

The repetition-penalty sampler and the DRY sampler each pre-size a ring buffer to the **raw client-supplied count**, with no clamp to the context size or any other cap. The request schema hard-limits `repeat_last_n` and `dry_penalty_last_n` only to `0 .. INT32_MAX` (`tools/server/server-schema.cpp:126` and `:153`), and the value flows unclamped into sampler initialization. The buffer is **value-initialized (zero-filled)**, so every page is actually committed.

A single unauthenticated request therefore forces a huge allocation at slot launch (sampler init), **before any token is generated** (so `n_predict: 1` is enough): Claude results

| trigger (fields in the request body) | buffer(s) allocated | size at `INT32_MAX` |
|---|---|---|
| `repeat_penalty:1.1, repeat_last_n:2147483647` | `prev` ring buffer (`llama_token`, 4 B) | **~8.6 GB** |
| `dry_multiplier:1.0, dry_base:1.1, dry_penalty_last_n:2147483647` | `dry_repeat_count` (`int`) **+** `last_tokens` ring buffer | **~17 GB** |

On a default deployment (Linux memory overcommit on, no cap) the zero-fill commits the pages and the OOM-killer `SIGKILL`s the server: a single request kills a typical 2–16 GB container/VM, and a handful of concurrent requests exhausts any host. Under a memory cap (`ulimit -v` / cgroup) the allocation throws `std::bad_alloc`, which the server catches (`server-context.cpp:1782`) and turns into a `400`, so the server survives — but that is a fragile, deployment-dependent mitigation, not a bound.

Measured (CPU build, `ulimit -v 5000000` so the blow-up fails safely; `VmHWM` = peak resident):

```
baseline                                             VmHWM  598 MB
repeat_penalty=1.0, repeat_last_n=2e9  (DISABLED)     200,   Δ +0 MB     <- ablation: no alloc
repeat_penalty=1.1, repeat_last_n=1e8  (enabled)      200,   Δ +382 MB   <- committed ~= 1e8 * 4 B
repeat_penalty=1.1, repeat_last_n=2e9  (enabled)      400 "Failed to initialize samplers: std::bad_alloc"
dry_multiplier=0.0, dry_penalty_last_n=2e9 (DISABLED) 200,   Δ +0 MB     <- ablation: no alloc
dry_multiplier=1.0, dry_penalty_last_n=1e8 (enabled)  200,   Δ +384 MB   <- committed, proportional

title: Eval bug: qwen35 dirty-ctx full-restore in test-recurrent-state-rollback fails deterministically (CPU+CUDA, q8_0+f16) while arch is whitelisted
body:
## Summary

`test-recurrent-state-rollback` fails **deterministically** on a qwen35 (QWEN35 arch) model at the *dirty-ctx full-restore* path — on **both CPU and CUDA backends, both q8_0 and f16** — while the architecture gate `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` (`src/llama-arch.cpp:1105` in v0.4.1) lists `LLM_ARCH_QWEN35` as supported. Same family of gap as #28019 (qwen4exp) and #28461 (Kimi-K3 bounded support), so filing separately with a clean matrix.

## Environment

- llama.cpp **v0.4.1**
- Model: Qwen3.5-0.8B (smoke GGUF), tested in **q8_0** and **f16**
- Host A: Ubuntu, x86_64 (CPU path, `-ngl 0`)
- Host B: VM with Tesla P4 (sm_61), CUDA 12.9 (`-ngl 99`, `-c 512`)

## Reproduction / observed matrix

Run `tests/test-recurrent-state-rollback` against the model:

| # | quant | backend | result |
|---|-------|---------|--------|
| E1 | q8_0 | CPU | RC=1 — `dirty-ctx logits mismatch at position 6, token 0 (6.24078 != 8.16677)` |
| E2 | q8_0 | CUDA | RC=1 — same position, same token |
| E3 | f16 | CPU | RC=1 — `6.18489 != 8.17146` |
| E4 | f16 | CUDA | RC=1 — `6.18417 != 8.17025` |

Four (quant × backend) combos produce the **same position, same token, same magnitude** (~6.18 vs ~8.17; f16 vs q8_0 differ by only 0.06) ⇒ neither quantization noise nor the CUDA/Pascal path is the cause.

## Where it fails in code

`test_rollback()`'s **dirty-ctx branch** (`tests/test-recurrent-state-rollback.cpp:373–415`): decode noise → `llama_memory_seq_rm(..., rollback_pos, -1)` → `ckpt.load_tgt(ctx_dirty, 0, 0)` (full restore, flags=0) → replay mismatches.

The `PARTIAL_ONLY` branch and the clean-dst path **pass** — so coverage of the full-restore-into-dirty-ctx path for this arch looks incomplete rather than numerically off.

## Expected / question

Qwen3.5-0.8B is in the rs-rollback whitelist, so I expected all four rollback paths to hold. Options as I see them: either complete the full-restore path for QWEN35, or drop it from `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` until then (as #28461 did boundary work for Kimi-K3). We have worked around it on our side by avoiding `seq_rm`/state reuse entirely (rebuild per request), but wanted to report the whitelist-vs-implementation gap while it's cleanly isolated.

title: [RFC] Inkling architecture support with CPU-first implementation, split from #25731
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).

- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Proposal to implement the Inkling architecture (thinkingmachines Inkling / Inkling-Small, audio + vision + text MoE) upstream, CPU-only first, with backend support in follow-up PRs, per the large-change policy in CONTRIBUTING. This implements #27359.

### Relationship to #25731

#25731 (open draft) implements the full stack in one PR (70 files, +4,120/−126).  It was flagged at submission for bundling multiple backends.  The latest maintainer signal re-states the CPU-first policy.  This RFC proposes the same architecture work in the guideline-compliant shape, wherein CPU-only will be implemented first, with backends in follow-up PRs. Scoping for this RFC was done against #25731's public diff and any reuse of its tensor mapping will be credited. We can coordinate this however the maintainers prefer.  

### Motivation

• Inkling and Inkling Small each have 500k+ downloads on HF. 
• Today there is no official llama.cpp support, and it runs only on third-party fork builds.  

### Possible Implementation

• **PR 1 CPU:** Converter (`conversion/inkling.py`, arch registration, tensor mapping), graph build, hparams/KV-cache handling for the mixed local-SWA/full-attention layers with relative bias, CPU op adjustments (sconv), chat parser + template, mtmd preprocessing (hmlp vision, dmel audio), `test-llama-archs` fixture + op tests, with no backend changes. (~2.8k lines scoped against the public reference diff.)
• **PR 2 CUDA:** The banded flash-attention kernel and its test suite.
• **PR 3+ Vulkan/Misc:** Remaining backend bits and performance follow-ups.

### Questions for Maintainers

Are there any concerns with proceeding with PR 1 as scoped?

title: Misc. bug: Backend Top-K output buffer is still allocated at full vocabulary width
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 1, commit 66fba63af)
built with GNU 16.2.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Observed behavior

In `src/llama-sampler.cpp`, `llama_sampler_top_k_backend_apply()` reduces the logits and candidate IDs to `k` elements. In `src/llama-context.cpp`, `copy_tensor_async_rows()` copies only `ggml_nbytes(tensor)` bytes and records `ggml_nelements(tensor)` in the corresponding row’s `*_count`.

However, `llama_context::output_reserve()` allocates space for the raw logits, sampled logits, sampled probabilities, and candidate IDs using `n_vocab * n_outputs_max`. With a backend sampler configured, the sampling output alone reserves two vocabulary-width float arrays, one vocabulary-width token ID array, and one sampled token per row. Space for the full raw logits is also reserved even when this backend-sampling path does not copy them.

In `decode()`, the sampling output still uses `n_vocab` as the destination row stride. `copy_tensor_async_rows()` writes to `base + row * stride`: each row copies `k` sampled logits and `k` candidate IDs, leaving up to approximately `n_vocab - k` unused positions in each array. The sampled-output getters locate rows using `row * n_vocab`. When reordering occurs, `output_reorder()` swaps sampling arrays one full `n_vocab`-wide row at a time.

### Results

**Allocation formula and measured capacity:** Let `V = n_vocab` and `R = n_outputs_max`. With both `float` and `llama_token` occupying 4 bytes, the sampling output reserves `12 * V * R + 4 * R` bytes, while the raw logits reserve another `4 * V * R` bytes. This excludes embeddings, layer inputs, the model, the KV cache, and backend workspaces.

**Reproduction (2026-09-27):** The reproduction program is in the first comment. Both backends used the same commit, the same Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 GGUF (`V=248320`), and the same token sequence. For each K/R configuration, only the execution backend differed. The parameters were `n_ctx=2048`, `n_batch=n_ubatch=64`, `n_seq_max=1`, and `n_outputs_max=n_outputs_max_per_seq=R`. The last token returned by `llama_tokenize("Hello", add_special=true)` was repeated at R consecutive positions, with output requested at every position. Each run used a fresh process. In all six runs, `llama_decode` returned 0, the number of output rows equaled R, and every row’s logits and candidate counts equaled K.

| K | R | Logits / candidate count per row | Host output buffer | Buffer type |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 8 | 1 | 8 / 8 | 3,973,124 B | CPU |
| 8 | 64 | 8 / 8 | 254,279,936 B | CPU |
| 80 | 64 | 80 / 80 | 254,279,936 B | CPU |
| 8 | 1 | 8 / 8 | 3,973,124 B | CUDA_Host |
| 8 | 64 | 8 / 8 | 254,279,936 B | CUDA_Host |
| 80 | 64 | 80 / 80 | 254,279,936 B | CUDA_Host |

At a fixed R of 64, increasing K from 8 to 80 increases the actual logits and candidate counts per row tenfold, while the host output buffer capacity remains unchanged on both CPU and CUDA.

### First Bad Commit

[d3dce4e0a5f2fd497a312a3152f2eab939f0d519](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/d3dce4e0a5f2fd497a312a3152f2eab939f0d519) (#17004) introduced ggml_top_k(..., k), copying based on the tensor’s actual byte size, and allocating sampling arrays using n_vocab * n_outputs_max.

[eef375ce167cf36d8ed2cf347be95a7a7a90fb5e](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/eef375ce167cf36d8ed2cf347be95a7a7a90fb5e) (#18811) later removed the cpu_logits condition, changing logits_size = (has_logits && cpu_logits) ? ... : 0 to logits_size = has_logits ? ... : 0.

title: Official Windows prebuilt binaries crash with heap corruption (0xC0000374) on Windows 11 Insider build 26220 — LLVM OpenMP vs MSVC OpenMP
body:
## Bug Description

Official llama.cpp Windows prebuilt binaries (both `bin-win-vulkan-x64` and `bin-win-cpu-x64`) **crash with heap corruption (0xC0000374 / STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) when loading ANY GGUF model** on Windows 11 Insider Preview build 26220. The crash happens during model load with **no console output at all** (not even backend initialization logs). All tested versions crash: b9601, b10608, b10620.

A locally-built/third-party llama.cpp runtime that links **MSVC OpenMP (VCOMP140)** instead of **LLVM OpenMP (libomp)** works perfectly on the same machine — strongly suggesting the issue is **LLVM OpenMP runtime incompatibility with this Windows build**.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro Insider Preview **Build 26220** (10.0.26220)
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 7840HS (Zen 4, supports AVX-512)
- GPU: AMD Radeon 780M (RDNA3, integrated)
- RAM: 32 GB DDR5
- llama.cpp: official prebuilt `llama-b10620-bin-win-vulkan-x64.zip` / `llama-b10620-bin-win-cpu-x64.zip` (also reproduced with b9601, b10608)

## Steps to Reproduce

```
llama-cli.exe -m <any gguf> -ngl 0 -p "hi" -n 4
```

Any model, any parameters: tested with Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M (2.4 GB) and Qwen3.5-9B Q6_K (7.4 GB). Also reproduced with `llama-bench` and `llama-server`.

## What Was Ruled Out

- **Model files** — `llama-tokenize` loads the same GGUFs fine; multiple models from different sources all crash
- **Multi-threading** — `-t 1` still crashes
- **MMAP** — `--no-mmap` still crashes
- **Memory allocation size** — `-c 1 -b 1` (minimal buffers) still crashes
- **AVX-512 code path** — removing all AVX-512 variant DLLs (zen4/icelake/cascadelake/cooperlake/sapphirerapids/skylakex/alderlake/cannonlake) to force AVX2 still crashes
- **VC++ runtime** — copying the bundled MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140 DLLs into the package dir changes nothing
- **libomp version** — replacing with b9601's `libomp140.x86_64.dll` still crashes

## Key Evidence (DLL swap experiments)

1. **Removing `libomp.dll`** → error changes to `0xC0000135` (DLL not found) → the official build **hard-depends on LLVM OpenMP**.
2. **Replacing `libomp.dll` with MSVC `vcomp140.dll`** (official, from System32) → error changes to `0xC0000139` (entry point not found) → `ggml-base.dll` imports these **LLVM/Intel OpenMP ABI symbols** which VCOMP140 does not export:

```
__kmpc_barrier
__kmpc_dispatch_deinit
__kmpc_dispatch_init_4
__kmpc_dispatch_next_4
__kmpc_end_reduce_nowait
__kmpc_fork_call
__kmpc_reduce_nowait
```

3. **LM Studio / Bionic's bundled llama.cpp** (built with MSVC OpenMP, `VCOMP140.dll`) loads and runs the exact same models on the exact same machine with zero issues.

## Crash Event Log (Windows Application Error)

```
Faulting application name: llama-cli.exe, version: 0.0.0.0
Faulting module name: ntdll.dll, version: 10.0.26100.9223
Exception code: 0xc0000374
Fault offset: 0x0000000000117eb5
```

## Hypothesis

LLVM OpenMP runtime (libomp) appears to corrupt the heap during model loading on Windows 11 Insider build 26220 (possibly an interaction between LLVM OpenMP's thread-pool/barrier initialization and this Windows build). Official prebuilt binaries therefore cannot run on this system, while MSVC-OpenMP builds are unaffected.

## Suggested Actions

- Please investigate LLVM OpenMP compatibility with recent Windows Insider builds, or
- Consider publishing Windows builds linked against MSVC OpenMP (VCOMP140) as an alternative, which would also match what LM Studio ships.

Happy to provide more logs or run additional experiments (e.g. WER full dumps) if helpful.

title: Eval bug: [Vulkan] GGML_ABORT cache_k_l0 in Vulkan buffer on SWA models — regression 2.40/2.41 vs 2.39
body:
### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

title: Feature Request: Add support for K2 Horizon (0.9B, 3.7B, 7B, 32B, 36B MoVA)
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

We'd like to add K2 Horizon to llama.cpp. It's our model family at IFM (MBZUAI), and there are five sizes: 0.9B, 3.7B, 7B, 32B and a 36B MoE that uses MoVA. They all use the same architecture, so it's one `k2-horizon` arch and one converter for all of them.

We already have it working on our fork: https://github.com/ifm-ai/llama.cpp/tree/model/K2Horizon

GGUFs for all sizes are on Hugging Face: (https://huggingface.co/collections/IFM/k2-horizon-quantization)


### Motivation

Quite a few people are already using the fork, but that means building a separate llama.cpp and waiting on us every time upstream moves. We'd much rather have it in main so it works everywhere llama.cpp does, and we can stop maintaining a fork.

The good news is it's not a big change. The base is a regular Llama-style decoder. The dense models add two small things: RMSNorm is applied in groups over the hidden dim (with one full-length weight), and there's an optional softplus gate on the attention output before `o_proj`. Both are a few existing ops in the graph. The 36B also has a DeepSeek-V3-style MoE FFN, which goes straight through `build_moe_ffn`, plus MoVA, which is the one part that's actually new.

### MoVA

MoVA is "mixture of value experts". In the sparse layers of the 36B, instead of a single V projection, each token picks 4 out of 64 value projections through a small router. It then mixes them: `V = Σ w_k · silu(W_k x)`. Q and K are untouched.

We tried to make it look as much like the existing MoE code as possible:

- All 64 expert matrices are stacked into one 3D tensor at conversion time, so in the graph it's a single `ggml_mul_mat_id` that only computes the 4 selected experts per token. It's the same trick `build_moe_ffn` uses, so it runs on every backend with no new ops.
- The router follows the MoE FFN's conventions: sigmoid scores, a bias that only affects which experts get selected, and the mixing weights taken from the unbiased scores, then normalized and scaled. Because of that we reuse the existing gating/norm/scale keys. The only new keys are `attention.value_expert_count` and `attention.value_expert_used_count`.
- The mixed V is what goes into attention, so the KV cache doesn't change at all. It's the same size and layout as any other model. The extra cost is only in the V projection.

It lives in one helper, `build_routed_value`, in `src/models/k2-horizon.cpp`. The tensors are currently named `attn_v_gate` (router) and `attn_v_exps` (experts). We're happy to switch to names that mirror the FFN MoE ones (`attn_v_gate_inp`, `attn_v_exp_probs_b`, ...) if you prefer, since we'd rather get that right before merging.

### Possible Implementation

Everything is on the fork: the converter (`conversion/k2_horizon.py` + gguf-py), the model (`src/models/k2-horizon.cpp`, built on the usual `build_*` helpers), the tokenizer, and the chat template with reasoning/tool call parsing for `llama-server --jinja`.

One thing worth mentioning about the tokenizer: the HF pre-tokenizer regex uses `\p{...}` classes, which `std::regex` can't handle on MSVC. So we wrote the splitter by hand in `unicode.cpp`, the same way the llama3 one is done, and added cases to `test-unicode`.

We've tested on CPU and CUDA.

If it's easier to review, we can split this into a few smaller PRs (the jinja fix, the tokenizer, the model, then chat parsing). Just let us know what works best.

How to contribute to make the list more complete:

3. Test your implementation with `test-backend-ops -o <op>`
4. If it passes test for the op, create a PR.
5. Mention performance tests in the PR if they exist (via `test-backend-ops perf -o <op>`)

Notes:
1. The ops suffixed with _BACK are related to training which is WIP and does not require immediate attention

3. This list can be temporarily out of sync, you can check support by first running `test-backend-ops -o <op>` on master to confirm 
4. Please do not ask to be assigned a particular task, make the PR first if you think it will be useful


### Motivation

Feature parity between backends is always desirable and it's easy to test the implementation, making it an ideal good first issue.

title: Misc. bug: ggml-cpu : CPU backend score ignores OS XSAVE support -> SIGILL when CPUID advertises AVX but OS does not enable it

version: 0.3.0-dev (build 10766, commit 9400c8946)

### Operating systems

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section), libllama (core library)

$ ./build/bin/test-backend-ops
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

ggml_backend_cpu_x86_score() in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/cpu-feats.cpp checks CPUID feature bits but not the OS-enabled XSAVE state (XCR0). Under GGML_BACKEND_DL, the loader can select an AVX/AVX512 variant on a system where the OS/hypervisor has not enabled that state, causing a SIGILL. title: Misc. bug: --cors-origins does not follow spec
body:
### Name and Version

$ llama-cli --version
version: 10360 (48d22e295)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
--cors-origins "moz-extension://f745c4ad-86bf-4062-b715-e26739741e4d,http://localhost:8042"
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

As per https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md this flag takes:
> comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS (default: *)
if set to special value 'localhost', reflect the Origin header only if it is localhost
(env: LLAMA_ARG_CORS_ORIGINS)

So I want to accept requests from localhost and a firefox extension

`--cors-origins "moz-extension://f745c4ad-86bf-4062-b715-e26739741e4d,http://localhost:8042"`

However this doesn't follow the spec

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Origin

> Specifies a single origin. If the server supports clients from multiple origins, it must return the origin for the specific client making the request.

So it SHOULD return the origin (only 1) if it patched the header that is received but https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/8e7f22b/tools/server/server-http.cpp#L292

returns the entire value pass AS-IS, this of course does not work correctly. 

The easiest fix is fixing the docs to mention only 1 origin can be specified, so people don't lose hours debugging why it's not working.

The proper fix would be to return the correct origin value based on the received origin header.

n/a

n/a

title: Eval bug: failed slot restore leaves corrupted K/V data that breaks subsequent inference
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10398, commit 8e7f22b67)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA
CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i7 14700F
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 12 GB

### Models

Original observation through Ollama:

* `Qwen3.5 2B Q8_0` (hybrid)

Primary `llama-server` reproduction:

* `Gemma 3 4B IT Q4_K_M`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I found this while intentionally corrupting a completed slot snapshot as part of a persistent-cache fault-injection test through Ollama.
I have not observed slot files becoming corrupted during normal save or restore operations.
The corrupted state is correctly rejected, but K/V data written before the validation failure can remain in the cache and affect subsequent inference.
In the reproducing case, later completions become empty, erasing the slot does not recover the process, and restarting `llama-server` does.

I reproduced the same behavior with stock `llama-server`, so this is not specific to Ollama.
`llama-completion` does not exercise this path because its prompt-cache path uses the whole-context state API, while this issue is in the per-sequence slot restore path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server`:

```bash
llama-server -m gemma-3-4b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --no-mmproj \
  --slot-save-path /tmp/slots \
  -np 1 -c 4096 -ngl all -fa on --no-webui
```

2. Process the prompt used in this reproduction:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.dumps({
      'prompt': 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the river bank. ' * 170,
      'n_predict': 1,
      'temperature': 0,
      'cache_prompt': True
  }))")"
```

This produced about 2382 prompt tokens.

Save slot 0:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/slots/0?action=save" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"good.bin"}'
```

The resulting state file was `170,469,452` bytes.

3. Corrupt 8 MiB starting at 14 MiB:

```bash
cp /tmp/slots/good.bin /tmp/slots/corrupt.bin

dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/slots/corrupt.bin \
  bs=1048576 count=8 seek=14 conv=notrunc
```

These offsets are specific to this saved state file. They caused some K/V data to be written to the backend buffers before validation failed on a later tensor header, at layer 29 in this run.

As controls, a truncated copy and loading the same state with the incompatible `-fa off` layout both failed before entering the K/V data-write loop. Neither affected subsequent inference.

4. Restore the corrupted state:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/slots/0?action=restore" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"corrupt.bin"}'
```

The restore correctly returns HTTP 400.

5. Send a short completion request:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Write one short sentence about the sea.","n_predict":32,"temperature":0,"cache_prompt":false}'
```

In the reproducing case, the relevant response fields are:

```text
tokens_predicted: 32
stop_type: "limit"
content: ""
```

6. Erase slot 0, then repeat the same completion request.

The response remains empty and the process remains affected.

7. Restart `llama-server`. Completions work normally again.

### Suspected cause

`state_read_data()` validates and writes K/V data layer by layer.
If validation fails on a later layer, earlier K/V data may already have been written into the backend buffers.

The rollback is asymmetric:

* whole-context restore uses `clear(true)`, which also clears the K/V buffers
* per-sequence restore uses `seq_rm()`, which removes cell metadata but leaves the underlying K/V data

This can leave corrupted K/V data in cells that are subsequently considered free.
Free cells are expected to be excluded by attention masking. In the reproduced path, corrupted f16 data can contain NaNs that are not neutralized by the masking operation.
A C API reproduction also confirmed NaN logits on CPU and showed that deferred buffer writes can be applied after the existing rollback.
PR #26051 made exceptions from `state_read_data()` enter the existing rollback path. For per-sequence restore, that path removes sequence metadata but does not clear K/V data written before the failure.

### Expected behavior

A failed per-sequence restore should leave later inference and other sequences usable. Restoring the previous contents of the target slot is not required.

### Related

* #26744 - stale K/V in freed cells affects attention through a separate Vulkan-specific mechanism
* #9173 - slot restore failure followed by failure in later processing
* #17527 / PR #17982 - fragmented restore failure before K/V data is written
* #23720 / PR #23981 - checkpoint restore failure involving internally generated checkpoint state

AI tools assisted with code investigation and analysis. I independently reproduced the issue and validated the technical claims in this report.

A minimal fix and regression test are working locally, and I can open a PR. 

### First Bad Commit

I do not believe this is a recent regression. The metadata-only per-sequence rollback predates #26051, and this reproduction reaches it through `state_read_data()` returning `false`.

### Relevant log output

```console
state_read_data: mismatched key type (1 != 248383823, layer 29)
llama_state_seq_load_file: error loading sequence state file: failed to restore kv cache
srv    send_error: task id = 5, error: Unable to restore slot: No available space in KV cache or invalid slot save file
```

The mismatched key value comes from the randomly corrupted bytes and therefore changes between runs.

title: Eval bug: --split-mode tensor crashes with GGML_ASSERT(bcj.nodes[i]) on second request (2x/3x Tesla P100, CUDA)
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.0-dev (build 1, commit 5266f24)
Built from a patched source tree: shinbunbun/llama-cpp-p100-patches (29 patches) applied on top of a pristine v0.4.0 checkout, per the project's documented apply process. None of the patches touch multi-GPU split, scheduler, or graph-reuse code — they are Pascal-specific kernel/AllReduce-transport patches (quantized matmul kernels, enabling the internal AllReduce path on sm_60, and a copy-engine stream fix). I have not yet tested against a pristine (unpatched) v0.4.0 build — will update if I do.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`--split-mode tensor` loads successfully and serves the first request on a slot without issue. The **second** request on the same (re-used) slot reliably crashes the process with a GGML_ASSERT inside the meta-backend, during the first decode of that new request.

This reproduces identically with 3 GPUs (`-ts 1/1/1`) and with exactly 2 GPUs (`-ts 1/1`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`, confirmed applied via `systemctl show -p Environment`). Does **not** reproduce under `--split-mode layer` — ran 3 sequential requests back-to-back on that mode with otherwise identical flags/model/context and all completed cleanly.

Also ruled out as causes (isolated one variable at a time):
- Context size — reproduces at both `--ctx-size 256000` and `--ctx-size 8192`.
- MTP / speculative decoding — reproduces with `--spec-type draft-mtp` fully removed from the command line (this report). Note: MTP enabled is a *separate*, independently-reproducing crash on the *first* request, going through `common_speculative_impl_draft_mtp::process` — did not investigate further since it's a distinct code path.
- Prompt caching / LCP slot similarity — reproduces with `--no-cache-prompt --slot-prompt-similarity 0` set.

Launch command (2-GPU variant):

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 /opt/llama.cpp-p100/build/bin/llama-server
-m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf
-sm tensor
-ts 1/1
-ngl 99
--ctx-size 8192
-fa on
--fit off
--cache-type-k q8_0
--cache-type-v q8_0
--parallel 1
--cache-ram 0
--no-cache-prompt
--slot-prompt-similarity 0
--jinja
--reasoning on
--reasoning-budget 7500
--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080


Steps:
1. Start server as above.
2. Send one completion request. It completes successfully (e.g. 291 graphs reused, clean `slot release`).
3. Send a second completion request on the same slot. Crashes immediately on `launch_slot_` / first decode.

- This may be related to #22307 (assert inside the meta-backend's split-tensor path, also request-2-not-request-1, also `-sm layer` unaffected) — different assert line/message (`ggml-backend-meta.cpp:1299`, `size == ggml_nbytes(tensor)`, ROCm) — and to #24549 (unmerged draft: stale graph reuse under `SPLIT_MODE_TENSOR` leaving dangling per-device tensor references) — different repro shape (that PR's case is two contexts sharing memory via MTP/EAGLE3; this report has MTP fully disabled, single context/slot, plain sequential requests). Flagging both as possibly-related rather than assuming either is a duplicate.
- Separate anomaly, possibly worth its own issue: restricting to exactly 2 visible CUDA devices (confirmed via `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` and `systemctl show -p Environment`) still logs `internal AllReduce init failed (n_devices != 2?)` before falling back to the butterfly path — per the AllReduce feature's documented scope (2 GPUs, FP32, tensors ≤256 KB), the 2-GPU case should be exactly the case it succeeds on. Have not yet dug into `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/allreduce.cu` to see what else the init might be gating on (dtype/tensor-size preconditions in this model/config, maybe).

title: Eval bug: Metal: per-file mmap mapping spans CPU-resident tensors, so a 27 GiB lazy-read table between GPU tensors counts against the GPU working set (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next OOM)
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11049, commit fa95fd1f8), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64 (Metal, Release). This is master plus #26004 and #28243 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP). The code involved (`llama_model_loader::get_mapping_range` and its caller in `llama-model.cpp`) is unchanged on master `d834d44e6` (2026-09-26).

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M4 Max, 128 GB unified memory, `iogpu.wired_limit_mb=114688` (`recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize = 120259.08 MB`)

### Models

unsloth `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL` (4 shards, 103.7 GiB), as downloaded

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With `mmap`, each shard is handed to Metal as one `buffer_from_host_ptr` covering the byte range from the first to the last GPU-assigned tensor in that file (`get_mapping_range`). Any tensor that sits *between* GPU tensors in the file is inside that range, even if it is CPU-resident, and it counts toward the GPU working set.

unsloth's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUFs place `per_layer_token_embd.weight` (27,465 MiB, lazy-read on the CPU: `tensor per_layer_token_embd.weight (size = 27465 MiB) lazy read enabled`) 5th in the first data shard, with GPU tensors on both sides. The Metal mapping therefore carries an extra ~26.8 GiB that the GPU never reads:

| file | MTL0_Mapped total | CPU_Mapped |
|---|---|---|
| UD-Q4_K_XL, as shipped | 47,549.79 + 47,088.71 + 11,527.99 = **106,166 MiB** | 644.14 + 27,465.95 |
| same tensors, PLE table moved to the end of the file (bit-identical, verified per-tensor sha256) | 47,417.16 + 31,283.38 = **78,701 MiB** | 644.14 + 27,465.95 |
| UD-IQ4_XS, as shipped (same layout) | 47,526.56 + 41,805.60 = 89,332 MiB | 644.14 + 27,465.95 |

The difference, 27,466 MiB, is exactly the size of the PLE table.

Consequences on a 128 GB Mac:

- `llama-server -m <Q4_K_XL> -md <MTP head> --spec-type draft-mtp -c 262144` with f16 KV: during load, `ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5`, `Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)`, then `failed to load draft model`.
- With `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` it starts, but every request fails with the same OOM, then `decode: failed to process speculative batch` (HTTP 500), while process RSS is only ~85 GiB.
- IQ4_XS has the same inflation and only just stays under the limit.

After moving the table to the end of the file (a plain gguf-py rewrite, no requantisation), f16 KV at 262,144 + MTP loads and serves. RSS is ~87 GiB idle and ~110 GiB at 200K tokens, and speed and output are unchanged.

`--lazy-mode off` doesn't help. The table then becomes resident as well, and it is still inside the Metal range.

### Suggested fix

In `get_mapping_range` / the `buffer_from_host_ptr` loop, split a file's range into several host-ptr buffers wherever there is a large gap of non-GPU tensors (or at least skip tensors that belong to a CPU/lazy context), rather than one `[first, last)` span per file. This would also help any other model whose GGUF interleaves large CPU-only tensors (e.g. with `-ot ... =CPU`) with offloaded ones.

A converter-side mitigation would also work: write large CPU-destined tensors such as `per_layer_token_embd` last. I can share the repack script if useful.

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression as far as I know: the single-range mapping is long-standing. It only becomes visible with a multi-GiB CPU tensor in the middle of a file.

### Relevant log output

```
ggml_metal_device_init: recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize  = 120259.08 MB
add: tensor per_layer_token_embd.weight (size = 27465 MiB) lazy read enabled
load_tensors:   CPU_Mapped model buffer size =   644.14 MiB
load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 47549.79 MiB
load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 47088.71 MiB
load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 11527.99 MiB
load_tensors:   CPU_Mapped model buffer size = 27465.95 MiB
...
E ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
E error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
E llama_model_load: error loading model: vector
E common_speculative_init_result: failed to load draft model, '.../mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-shared-Q8_0.gguf'
```

title: bug: the json-schema/GBNF grammar builder does not bound the repetition count — a contradictory or huge `min*` makes it allocate unboundedly and OOM-kills the server
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
( ulimit -v 3000000; llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 1024 --no-webui ) python3 repro_llamacpp_minitems_oom.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Script:  [repro_llamacpp_grammar_repetition_oom.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/855b27802f3c49edc5d85496f828ebdf#file-repro_llamacpp_grammar_repetition_oom-py)

A `response_format` / `json_schema` request whose schema is an **array with `minItems` greater than `maxItems`**, a contradictory but well-formed schema, the kind of thing a client produces by mistake, makes the json-schema → GBNF grammar builder attempt an **unbounded allocation**. 

On a normally-configured server (no memory limit) this drives resident memory to many gigabytes and the process is **OOM-killed**: the whole server dies, every in-flight and future request fails, and it must be restarted. A single unauthenticated request is enough.

Measured (fresh server per row, RSS sampled once per second):

| schema | peak RSS | result |
|---|---|---|
| `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":10,"maxItems":2}` | **11,447 MB** | process **Killed (OOM)**, server dead |
| `minItems:3, maxItems:2` (contradiction by 1) | (capped run) | `std::bad_alloc` when the server's virtual memory is `ulimit`-capped to 3 GB — i.e. the same unbounded allocation, merely caught by the OS limit |
| `minItems:2, maxItems:10` (valid) | 597 MB | 200, fine |
| `minItems:5, maxItems:5` (valid) | 597 MB | 200, fine |

So a valid array schema costs ~0.6 GB; flipping `minItems`/`maxItems` so that `minItems > maxItems` sends it to 11+ GB and death.

**The same defect has several entry points** (all measured on a memory-capped server, where the blow-up surfaces as `std::bad_alloc` / "failed to parse grammar" instead of OOM-killing the box):

| request | result (capped) | class |
|---|---|---|
| array `minItems:10, maxItems:2` | bad_alloc / grammar-fail 400 | contradiction (min>max) |
| string `minLength:10, maxLength:2` | bad_alloc / grammar-fail 400 | contradiction (min>max) |
| direct GBNF `root ::= "a"{10,2}` | hang / build | contradiction (N<M) |
| array `minItems:100000000` (valid, huge) | bad_alloc / grammar-fail 400 | huge lower bound |
| **controls:** array `minItems:2,maxItems:10`, string `maxLength:1e8`, array `maxItems:1e8` | 200 | upper bounds are fine |

So it is one root cause — the repetition-count arithmetic in the builder is neither guarded against `min > max` (which underflows in an unsigned type) nor capped for a large lower bound reached through arrays (`minItems`), strings (`minLength`), and direct GBNF `{M,N}` (object `minProperties` was inconsistent across runs and is left out). Upper bounds (`maxItems`/`maxLength`) are handled fine; only the required-count (lower) side blows up. 

With a memory limit in place the failure surfaces as `parse: error parsing grammar: std::bad_alloc` (HTTP 400) and the server survives, which only confirms that the trigger is an over-large allocation the OS limit truncates; the default deployment has no such limit and is OOM-killed.

title: Misc. bug: `/infill` does not validate prompt token ids, it accepts out-of-range ids that `/completion` rejects
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` (n_vocab 151,936).

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 --no-webui python3 repro_llamacpp_infill_oob.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137 --vocab 151936
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Repro script: [repro_llamacpp_infill_oob.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/b54b3e622e63e51c1508b6cc429ed365#file-repro_llamacpp_infill_oob-py)

When `prompt` is supplied as an array of token ids, `/completion` and `/v1/completions` validate that every id is in range and reject an out-of-range one with `400 "Prompt contains invalid tokens"`. `/infill` performs no such check: the same out-of-range id is accepted with `200` and fed into the model.

```
POST /v1/completions  {"prompt": [152936], "max_tokens": 4}
400  {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Prompt contains invalid tokens","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

POST /infill  {"input_prefix":"def f():","input_suffix":"return x","prompt":[152936],"n_predict":4}
200  {"content":"\n<tool_call>import sys", ...}
```

An id `>= n_vocab` (or negative) is not a valid token. Passing it into the model's context is undefined — on the inputs tried it produced output rather than crashing, but that is not a guarantee; the other routes treat it as a client error for good reason, and `/infill` should match them.

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

repro script: [repro_llamacpp_grammar_amplification.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/bbf2a82b541c34f8d0e8fe4c1805e743#file-repro_llamacpp_grammar_amplification-py)

A `response_format` / `json_schema` request whose schema contains a large `enum` causes the json-schema → GBNF grammar construction to take **superlinear** time, and that work runs **synchronously on the serving slot** before generation starts. A single small request therefore pins a CPU core for tens of seconds and holds the slot the whole time; a handful of such requests occupies every slot and denies service to all other clients. No authentication is required and the request body is small.

Measured (`n_predict: 1`, so the wall time is essentially the grammar build): _done by Claude_

| `enum` size | request body | grammar-build wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | ~0.6 KB | 0.12 s |
| 1,000 | ~6 KB | 0.75 s |
| 10,000 | ~59 KB | **6.5 s** |
| 50,000 | ~300 KB | **36 s** |
| 100,000 | ~600 KB | **> 58 s (timed out)** |

The time grows much faster than the input: a ~600 KB request takes **58+ seconds** of one pinned core, and larger enums scale to minutes. The build happens on the slot thread, so for its whole duration that slot answers nothing else, and every request already queued behind it waits.

### Where it comes from

The json-schema → GBNF converter expands an `enum` into grammar alternations and appears to do work that is superlinear in the number of members (e.g. repeated string building / rule construction), all before the request is admitted to generation. There is no cap on `enum` size, no time budget on grammar construction, and the build is not off the hot serving path.

title: Misc. bug: llama-server does not cap logprobs / top_logprobs (n_probs)
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, build b6002-era master (git `4b1a27f`, reported as `version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), built from source on Linux x86_64 (GCC 11.5), CPU backend, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`.


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 --no-webui
python3 repro_llamacpp_unbounded_logprobs.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This is prob an obvious and apparent issue, but you can try reproduce it with [repro_llamacpp_unbounded_logprobs.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/d8402faa6c6814ab14ec6b6d4d7c0f9d#file-repro_llamacpp_unbounded_logprobs-py)

The number of per-token probabilities returned for `logprobs` / `top_logprobs` (internally `n_probs`) is bounded **only by the vocabulary size**, not by any small cap. A single `/v1/completions` request can therefore be amplified into an enormous response and a correspondingly large amount of CPU (a full-vocabulary sort + JSON serialization per generated token) and memory.

Measured on the CPU build, `Qwen2.5-0.5B` (vocab 151,936), `max_tokens: 8`:

| `logprobs` | response size | wall time | `top_logprobs` per token |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 4.7 KB | 0.12 s | 5 |
| 1,000 | 728 KB | 0.31 s | 1,000 |
| 100,000 | **75 MB** | **5.6 s** | 100,000 |
| 200,000 | **115 MB** | **8.1 s** | 151,936 (clamped to vocab) |

So `logprobs: 200000` on an 8-token completion returns a **115 MB** JSON in **8 s**. The amount scales linearly with `max_tokens` as well: `max_tokens: 512, logprobs: 200000` would produce a response on the order of **7 GB** and minutes of CPU, from one request whose own body is a few hundred bytes. There is no authentication requirement and the OpenAI-compatible route accepts it.

For comparison, the OpenAI API caps `top_logprobs` at 20, and vLLM caps it (`max_logprobs`, default 20), refusing larger values with a 400.

title: SYCL: DFlash2 draft model triggers GPU driver TDR reset (VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED) on dual Arc Pro B70
body:
## Summary

Loading a DFlash2 draft model (`--model-draft`) on the SYCL backend against dual Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs causes a GPU driver TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) event — Windows force-resets the GPU driver — rather than a normal crash or clean load. The process disappears with no application-level error logged; the only trace is a `LiveKernelEvent` (Bug Check `0x141` = `VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED`) in the Windows Application event log, occurring on both GPUs across repeated attempts. GPU driver status recovers to `OK` afterward, but the server never comes up.

## Environment

- Build: `b10883` (commit `91f6a6cf3`), official Windows SYCL x64 binary, `version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10883, commit 91f6a6cf3)`
- Hardware: 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (32GB each)
- OS: Windows (native), Level-Zero runtime, driver `32.0.101.8805`
- Target: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q6_K_XL GGUF (unsloth)
- Draft: Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 Q8_0 GGUF (z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF)
- `--spec-type` not passed; auto-detected as `draft-dflash` from draft model metadata (confirmed in logs before the hang)

## Repro

```
set UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1
set ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1
set GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=0

llama-server.exe ^
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf ^
  --model-draft Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q8_0.gguf ^
  -ngl 99 -np 1 -c 131072 -t 8 ^
  --load-mode dio -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 ^
  -b 2048 -ub 2048 -fa on --jinja --reasoning off ^
  --metrics --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9019
```

No `--split-mode` flag is passed (default layer/pipeline split across the two GPUs) — this is not the tensor-parallel-specific issue reported separately for the CUDA backend (see linked issue).

## Observed

Console output reaches this point and then the process silently disappears (varies run-to-run exactly how far it gets before vanishing — sometimes right after tensor-warning lines, sometimes after the speculative implementation is registered):

```
I spec common_specu: auto-detected speculative type 'draft-dflash' from the draft model metadata
I srv    load_model: loading model '...Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf'
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: dflash requires ctx_other to be set (this warning is normal during memory fitting)
W operator(): failed to measure the memory of the extra model, fitting without it: failed to create llama_context from model
... (unused-tensor warnings for blk.64.* — expected, same as non-crashing loads)
I cmn          init: llama threadpool init, n_threads = 8
I common_speculative_init_result: loading draft model '...Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q8_0.gguf'
I srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 131072, kv_unified = 'false'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dflash'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=3, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=8, mask_token_id=248070, n_extract=5, sample_from_anchor=true
```
— then nothing. No further stdout/stderr, no application-error event (Event ID 1000), process no longer present in `tasklist`.

Windows Application event log (via `Get-WinEvent`), timestamped to match the hang, on every attempt (reproduced 3x with different process-launch methods — direct WSL exec, detached WSL background, and native PowerShell `Start-Process` — ruling out a launcher artifact):

```
Provider: Windows Error Reporting
Event ID: 1001
Event Name: LiveKernelEvent
Problem signature: P1: 141   (Bug Check 0x141 = VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED)
```

Multiple such events fired per attempt (both GPU device contexts affected, based on distinct P3 addresses corresponding to the two cards). `Get-WmiObject Win32_VideoController` reports `Status: OK` on both GPUs after each hang — the driver recovers, but the model never loads.

For comparison, the same target model with native MTP drafting (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) loads and serves normally on this exact hardware/build family (production config, no TDR events).

## Expected

DFlash2 should load and serve without hanging the GPU driver, matching the behavior of native MTP speculative decoding on the same hardware.

## Notes

- Not reproducible as a normal segfault/exception — no Application Error (Event ID 1000) is ever logged, only the driver-level TDR event, suggesting whatever DFlash2-specific kernel/operation is dispatched here enters a state the Level-Zero/SYCL driver cannot recover from within the timeout, rather than crashing outright.
- Happy to test a patched build or provide `sycl-ls` output / additional driver diagnostics if useful.

title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets
body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

title: Misc. bug: `usage.completion_tokens` counts only one choice, so it undercounts by a factor of `n` when `n > 1`
body:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 --no-webui
python3 repro_llamacpp_usage_undercount.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

For a request with `n > 1`, the server generates `n` independent completions but reports `usage.completion_tokens` for **only one** of them. The value is therefore an undercount of the tokens actually generated, by a factor of `n`, and `total_tokens` is wrong to match.

Measured, `max_tokens: 8`, `temperature: 0.8`, on `/v1/chat/completions`:

| `n` | choices returned (all distinct, each ~8 tokens) | `usage.completion_tokens` | actually generated |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 8 | 8 |
| 2 | 2 | **8** | 16 |
| 4 | 4 | **8** | 32 |

At `n=4` the server returned four different 8-token completions (32 tokens of real work) and reported `completion_tokens: 8`. The number does not grow with `n` at all.

The OpenAI API it mirrors defines `usage.completion_tokens` as the total across all `n` choices, so a client, or any accounting, rate-limiting or cost estimation keyed on `completion_tokens`, sees one quarter of the real generation cost at `n=4`.

please use this script for reproduction: [repro_llamacpp_usage_undercount.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/48977a938ef7f62b60a5b4fb01ce502b#file-repro_llamacpp_usage_undercount-py), with the command provided

title: Eval bug: gemma4-assistant MTP draft model fails to load — "invalid vector subscript" (regression: works on b9553, broken on   b9702/b9717)
body:
### Name and Version

 Affected (BROKEN):
  version: 9717 (8141e730f)   built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
  version: 9702 (968c43891)

  Last known good (WORKS):
  version: 9553 (9e3b928fd)   built with Clang 19.1.5 for Windows x86_64

  Official Windows CUDA 13.3 release builds.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Ryzen 7 5800X + 4070Ti Super 16gb

### Models

Speculative decoding (MTP draft) setup:
  - Target: gemma4-v2-Q8_0.gguf  (arch: gemma4)
  - Draft (MTP): gemma-4-12B-it-MTP-Q8_0.gguf  (arch: gemma4-assistant, nextn_predict_layers=4, block_count=4)

  Both from: https://huggingface.co/yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-composer2.5-v2-3.5x-tau2-GGUF

  The draft is the unsloth-converted GGUF of Google's official gemma-4-12B-it-assistant draft head.
  Gemma 4 MTP support landed in mainline via PR #23398 (merged 2026-06-07). The model author confirmed
  the files are correct and not built against any private fork. Also reproduced with the -MTP-BF16 variant.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

 Loading a gemma4-assistant MTP draft model for speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-mtp) crashes
  during model load with "invalid vector subscript". The main/target model loads fine — only the draft
  load crashes, so generation never starts.

  This is a REGRESSION. The exact same models + command load cleanly and work on b9553 (~2.5x speedup,
  lossless), but crash on b9702 and b9717. Something in the gemma4-assistant loader / context-init path
  regressed between b9553 and b9702.

  Command used (crashes on b9702/b9717, works on b9553 with the older flag names):

  b9702/b9717 (new flag names):
    llama-server -m gemma4-v2-Q8_0.gguf \
      --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-model gemma-4-12B-it-MTP-Q8_0.gguf \
      --spec-draft-ngl 99 --ctx-size 65536 -ngl 99 --flash-attn on --jinja

  b9553 (old flag names, WORKS):
    llama-server -m gemma4-v2-Q8_0.gguf \
      --model-draft gemma-4-12B-it-MTP-Q8_0.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp \
      --spec-draft-n-max 4 -ngl 99 -ngld 99 -fa on --jinja

  Key detail: the "invalid vector subscript" fires the instant `load_tensors: loading model tensors...`
  begins for the draft — before any tensor data is read. So the out-of-bounds is in the gemma4-assistant
  tensor-layout / model-build code, not in reading tensor data. Likely an out-of-range index over a
  per-layer array (block_count=4), e.g. attention.head_count_kv=[8,8,8,1] or
  sliding_window_pattern=[true,true,true,false], or nextn_predict_layers / embedding_length_out=3840 handling.

  The crash occurs AFTER the memory-fitting step (which harmlessly aborts with "n_gpu_layers already set
  by user to 99, abort"), at the actual draft load — so -fit off does not change it. The
  "Gemma4Assistant requires ctx_other to be set (this warning is normal during memory fitting)" line also
  appears on the working b9553 build and is harmless; the fatal regression is the "invalid vector subscript".

  Tried — all crash identically on b9702/b9717, both quants:
    b9702 + Q8_0 -> crash
    b9717 + Q8_0 -> crash
    b9717 + BF16 -> crash
    b9553 + Q8_0 -> WORKS

  So it is neither a file/quant issue nor a user-config issue. It is in the model loader and reproduces
  with any binary that loads this draft.

### First Bad Commit

 Not bisected. Good: b9553 (9e3b928fd). Bad: b9702 (968c43891) and b9717 (8141e730f).
  The regression was introduced somewhere in the b9553 -> b9702 range.

### Relevant log output
