title: [SYCL/xe] -cb pins GPU at gt-c0 on Battlemage, prevents idle power savings
body:
### What happened

When running `llama-server` with the SYCL backend on an Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage / `xe` driver), the `-cb` (continuous batching) flag keeps the GPU pinned in the active `gt-c0` power state with the clock at boost (2800 MHz) **continuously between requests**. The card never transitions to `gt-c6` deep sleep.

Over 8 days of uptime with the model loaded and serving sporadic requests, total GT idle residency was **197 seconds out of ~691,200** — 0.03% of the time. The card sustained ~50W idle draw, kept the fan audibly spinning, and held VRAM at ~72°C continuously.

`/slots` correctly reported `is_processing: false` between requests. CPU was at 0%. No actual inference was happening — the GPU's power state was simply stuck.

Dropping `-cb` (everything else identical) fixes it: the GT transitions to `gt-c6` within ~2 seconds of request completion. Wake latency on the next request is ~600ms (un-noticeable for inference workloads). VRAM cools from 72°C → 42°C, fan goes silent, power drops to <15W idle.

### Reproduction

```bash
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh

./build-sycl/bin/llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -c 524288 --parallel 2 -cb \
  --mlock --no-warmup \
  -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0
```

Make one chat completion request. Wait 30 seconds. Then check:

```bash
# Expected (without -cb): gt-c6 / 0 MHz / fan stops
# Observed (with -cb): gt-c0 / 2800 MHz / fan running
cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/tile0/gt0/gtidle/idle_status
cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/tile0/gt0/freq0/act_freq
sensors xe-pci-0300 | grep -E '^(pkg|vram|fan)'
```

`idle_residency_ms` under `/sys/.../gtidle/` confirms: barely advances with `-cb`, accumulates seconds-per-second without `-cb`.

### System

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31, `[8086:e223]`) |
| Driver | `xe` (replaced `i915` for Battlemage in kernel 6.11+) |
| Distro | Fedora Server, kernel 6.x |
| llama.cpp | latest master, `build-sycl` |
| Backend | SYCL via Intel Level Zero, oneAPI 2026.0 |
| Model | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at Q4_K_M, all layers on GPU |

### Root cause (best guess)

`-cb` keeps the SYCL command queue armed between requests so a new request can fuse into the in-flight batch with zero allocation overhead — that's its purpose. On the older `i915` driver, this was harmless because power-state transitions were gated on actual kernel execution, not queue residency. On the new `xe` driver, GT-c-state transitions are gated on the queue being drained, so an armed-but-idle queue holds the GT in `gt-c0` indefinitely.

The `-cb` behavior is correct in isolation. The `xe` driver behavior is also defensible in isolation. The interaction is what's broken — and it's not detectable from llama.cpp's perspective without sysfs inspection.

### Suggested resolution (any of these would help)

In increasing order of effort:

1. **Documentation note in the SYCL backend README:** add a line that `-cb` on the `xe` driver (Battlemage and later) currently prevents idle power savings. Recommend dropping `-cb` for low-throughput single-tenant deployments on those GPUs.
2. **Runtime warning:** if `/sys/bus/pci/drivers/xe` exists and `-cb` is enabled, log a one-line warning at startup. Users on `i915` would not see it.
3. **Idle-queue-drain:** after N seconds of no new requests, explicitly drain/destroy the SYCL queue and re-establish it on the next request. Wake cost is ~600ms in my testing — acceptable for the idle-power win on this driver path.

Option 1 alone would have saved me ~3 hours of diagnostics yesterday. The symptoms (nvtop showing 100% but `/slots` showing idle; high thermals but zero CPU) sent me down several wrong paths before I dropped to `/sys/class/drm` and found the GT-c-state evidence.

### Workaround

Drop `-cb`. `--parallel 2` (or higher) still allows concurrent request handling, just without cross-request decode-step fusion. The throughput cost is real only under sustained 10+ concurrent requests; for single-tenant or low-concurrency deployments on `xe`, dropping `-cb` is strictly better.

### Related — upstream `xe` driver

The deeper fix belongs in the `xe` kernel driver — it should drop the GT to a low-power state when no kernel is actively executing, regardless of queue residency. This matches `i915` behavior. I'll be filing a separate report against the `xe` driver tracker. This issue is filed here in the meantime because the documentation/warning fix is much faster and helps users immediately.

title: [CUDA] cublasCreate_v2 resource allocation failure on first inference — regression between b9553 and b9870
body:
Summary

On b9870, the server starts and loads the model successfully but crashes on the first inference request with a CUDA resource allocation failure in cublasCreate_v2. The same command and model work correctly on b9553.

Environment

| Attribute | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **OS** | Fedora Linux (kernel 7.0.14-201.fc44.x86_64) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU — 8 GB VRAM |
| **CUDA** | (check yours with `nvidia-smi`) |
| **Working version** | b9553 (9e3b928fd) |
| **Broken version** | b9870 (2d973636e) |

Model

- File: Qwopus3.6-35B-A3B-v1-MTP-IQ4_XS.gguf (Qwen3-based MoE, 19 GB, IQ4_XS quant)
- --n-cpu-moe 45 used to offload MoE expert layers to CPU

Command

llama serve \
  -m /path/to/Qwopus3.6-35B-A3B-v1-MTP-IQ4_XS.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -dev CUDA0 \
  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --no-mmap \
  -t 12 -c 128000 \
  --parallel 1 -ub 1024 -b 1024 \
  --cache-ram 24576 --cache-reuse 512 \
  --n-cpu-moe 45 \
  --port 8080 --host 127.0.0.1 --slots

Server output on b9870

0.11.622.432 W srv    load_model: cache_reuse is not supported by this context, it will be disabled
0.11.809.210 I srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 128000, kv_unified = 'false'
0.11.838.745 I srv          init: chat template supports preserving reasoning, consider enabling it via --reasoning-preserve
0.11.838.757 I srv  llama_server: model loaded
0.11.838.759 I srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
0.16.471.781 I slot get_availabl: id  0 | task -1 | selected slot by LRU, t_last = -1
0.16.471.856 I slot launch_slot_: id  0 | task 0 | processing task, is_child = 0
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:104: CUDA error
0.16.501.475 E CUDA error: the resource allocation failed
0.16.501.478 E   current device: 0, in function cublas_handle at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/../ggml-cuda/common.cuh:1477
0.16.501.479 E   cublasCreate_v2(&cublas_handles[device])

dmesg

llama[...]: segfault at 8 ip ...10ec965... error 4 in llama[...]

Same offset every crash — deterministic null pointer dereference triggered by the cuBLAS failure.

Analysis

The cuBLAS handle in cublas_handle (common.cuh:1477) is initialized lazily on first inference rather than at model load time. On an 8 GB GPU with a large MoE model and --n-cpu-moe, model weights fill the available VRAM during loading. When the first request arrives and cublasCreate_v2 attempts to allocate its workspace, no VRAM remains, causing the failure and subsequent crash.

On b9553 the same model and command work correctly on the same hardware, suggesting cuBLAS handle lifecycle or VRAM reservation changed between the two builds.

Steps to reproduce

1. Load a large MoE model with --n-cpu-moe on a GPU where VRAM is near-full after model load
2. Start the server — it reports model loaded and listening successfully
3. Send any inference request
4. Server crashes with cublasCreate_v2 resource allocation failure

Expected behaviour

cuBLAS handle is either pre-allocated at init time (before VRAM is fully committed to model weights), or the allocation failure is handled gracefully without crashing the server.

Workaround

Downgrade to b9553:
curl -L https://huggingface.co/buckets/ggml-org/install.sh/resolve/b9553/x86_64/linux/cuda/89/llama-app.zst | zstd -d > ~/.llama-app/llama && chmod +x ~/.llama-app/llama && ln -sf ~/.llama-app/llama ~/.local/bin/llama

title: Eval bug: SM_60 Quality Loss, FP32 math silently done in FP16, fix merged in two forks.
body:
### Name and Version

version: 9967 (4f37f5197)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Linux / CUDA / 4× Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (sm_60), dual Xeon, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.4. Tested on Ubuntu Server 26.04.

### Models

Qwen3.6-27B Q6_K (22,523,238,624 bytes) for the quality panel; Qwen3.6-4B dense and Darwin-36B-A3B (Qwen3.5-MoE arch) Q6_K for the speed legs.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

SM_60 currently gets put into a hardware accelerated fast-path by default, which uses a FP16 hardware accelerator. The problem is that some FP32 math is silently getting truncated to FP16 that shouldn't be, causing significant accuracy deviations from baseline (0.002298 median KL divergence vs FP32 reference/1-in-29 flipped top tokens).

The fix for this is to carve out SM_60 the same way SM_61 already is, bypassing the Fast Path gate, and keeping FP32 math at 32 bits as it should be.

## How to Fix

261- #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610
261+ #if defined(FP16_AVAILABLE) && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 610 && __CUDA_ARCH__ != 600

305-        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610) ||
305+        (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && fp16_available(cc) && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 610 && ggml_cuda_highest_compiled_arch(cc) != 600) ||

311-    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||
311+    return (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_NVIDIA(cc) && cc >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL && cc != 610 && cc != 600) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_AMD(cc) ||

TheTom (Tom Turney) has shipped: https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/releases/tag/tqp-v0.3.0 
https://github.com/TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant/pull/212 
spiritbuun has merged: https://github.com/spiritbuun/buun-llama-cpp/pull/80


## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Build stock llama.cpp using  `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=60`.
2. Generate the truth base, run `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base out.kld` with fp32 KV, FA off,
   on a patched build (fp32 arithmetic) — this is the step everyone skips.
3. Compare the stock vs patched runs against that base with `--kl-divergence`, 2048 ctx, 32 chunks.
4. Speed: `llama-bench` pp8192/tg32 @ d8192, patched vs unpatched, same host, nothing else
   on the GPUs.



### First Bad Commit

We followed the 610-only exemptions in their present form back through the 2024-era commits dc685be46 (#7188, FP32 FA vec kernel), 9b596417a (#7527, quantized KV for FA vec), and a818f3028 (#8075, MMQ-by-default) — sm_60 has been on the fast path the whole time,  no bisect needed.

### Relevant log output

What's below: same weights, f32 KV, FA is off on both sides; the only difference is stock fp16 arithmetic vs patched fp32 arithmetic, so it separates the arithmetic cost alone.

**Cell 0 (arithmetic-only delta, fp16 math vs fp32 math):**
median KLD **0.004962**, mean 0.023987, 99.9% 4.91, max 23.7, max Δp 98.9%,
**same-top 95.002%** — the arithmetic mode alone flips 1 in 20 greedy tokens, and about 1/1000
tokens gets its distribution basically replaced. This component is ~2× the attention-path
effect and was invisible to every prior measurement. 


Accuracy:
**Cells 1–3 **

| rung | unpatched median KLD | patched median KLD | same-top: unpatched → patched |
|---|---|---|---|
| f16-faoff | 0.002298  | **0.000001** | 96.47% → **99.89%** |
| f16-faon  | 0.002127 | **0.000000** | 96.45% → **99.93%** |
| q8-faon   | 0.002164 | **0.000005** | 96.52% → **99.80%** |


Performance:
pp8192 @ d8192, tg32 @ d8192, 4× P100 layer-split, same model:

| config | patched | unpatched | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| f16 KV prefill | 318.53 ± 0.53 t/s | 318.60 ± 0.35 t/s | **tie** |
| f16 KV tg      | 8.64 ± 0.00 t/s   | 8.51 ± 0.01 t/s   | +1.5% patched |
| q8_0 KV prefill| 312.60 ± 0.36 t/s | 312.52 ± 0.33 t/s | **tie** |
| q8_0 KV tg     | 8.46 ± 0.01 t/s   | 8.34 ± 0.01 t/s   | +1.4% patched |
Receipts: 
https://github.com/apollo-mg/Project-Apollo/tree/main/data/carveout_panel
https://github.com/apollo-mg/Project-Apollo/blob/main/data/Apollo%20Docs/Pascal_FAST_FP16_Carveout_Results.md

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Running MTP speculative decoding on the OpenVINO backend fails in every configuration I tried. Plain decode (same build, same model, no -md) works fine.

What I tried:

1. Target and draft both on OpenVINO (command above): crashes during graph compute with a MatMul shape error, then dumps core. See first log block. Looks like the draft graph's raw hidden-state input (3840-dim, fed from the target) doesn't get a dynamic token dimension, so the post-concat MatMul shape-infers wrong.

This matters: on this iGPU the OpenVINO backend prefills ~6.5x faster than Vulkan (917 vs 142 t/s, pp512, Gemma-4-12B Q4_0), but Vulkan+MTP decodes ~3x faster than OpenVINO (23.5 vs 8.1 t/s). title: Eval bug: GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa) dense-MLA CUDA path produces subtly corrupted output for ANY real transformer layer offloaded to GPU (partial coherent text mixed with garbage)
body:
### Name and Version

version: b10087 (1f66c3ce1)
Built with: cmake -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a-real -DGGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=ON

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (96GB VRAM each, SM120/compute capability 12.0)
- Intel Xeon 6787P (86 cores / 172 threads)
- Supermicro X14SBM-TP4F, 256GB DDR5 RAM
- CUDA Toolkit 12.9, nvidia-open driver

### Models

unsloth/GLM-5.2-GGUF, UD-IQ2_M (222.18 GiB, 2.53 BPW)
arch: glm-dsa, n_layer=78 (real transformer layers, blk.0-77), n_layer_all=79 (blk.78 is the MTP/NextN draft layer, tensors marked unused per #24770)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Testing with llama-server, single short prompt ("hello"), n_predict=30:

​```
-ngl 0  → correct, coherent English reasoning output
-ngl 1  → offloads output layer only → correct
-ngl 2  → offloads output layer + blk.78 (MTP layer, unused tensors) → correct
-ngl 3  → offloads output layer + blk.78 + blk.77 (first REAL transformer layer to hit GPU) → CORRUPTED

Exact garbled output at -ngl 3:
​```
"edReader is? Hmm, letAsc晴天Hello! I'm an AI assistant basedION6TK6T7QY7N5C0U"
Note this is NOT pure random noise — it contains a fully coherent English fragment ("Hello! I'm an AI assistant based") embedded within garbage tokens (random alphanumeric strings, an unrelated Chinese phrase). This pattern suggests a numerical/masking correctness bug (e.g. attention mask, RoPE application, or KV-cache indexing) in the dense-MLA CUDA path rather than random corruption, memory corruption, or a tokenizer/detokenizer issue.

Key observations ruling out other causes:
- No CUDA errors, NaN/Inf warnings, asserts, or crashes in logs — process completes normally with wrong output
- Reproducible with -DGGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=ON (rules out the Blackwell MMQ `sharedMemPerBlockOptin` driver bug, #23385)
- Reproducible with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a-real (real SASS, no PTX JIT — rules out JIT compilation issues)
- Reproducible with very short prompts (13 prompt tokens) and small n_predict — this does NOT require the "long prefill + high ubatch" conditions described in #23574, suggesting this may be a related-but-distinct instance of the same underlying dense-MLA-on-CUDA correctness issue, triggered simply by any real transformer layer running on GPU
- CPU-only inference (-ngl 0) is always correct
- The specific boundary is NOT about a "cursed" layer index — it's the transition from "no real attention layers on GPU" (-ngl ≤2, only output+MTP-draft-layer offloaded) to "at least one real attention layer on GPU" (-ngl ≥3)

This points to the dense-MLA CUDA kernel path used by GLM-5.2 (since the DSA lightning-indexer runtime isn't implemented yet, model falls back to `llama_model_deepseek2::graph` per #24770) having a correctness bug specific to Blackwell (SM120), or possibly affecting CUDA generally but only surfacing here due to GLM-5.2's specific MLA parameter shapes (q_lora_rank=2048, kv_lora_rank=512, key_length=576/mla=256, head_count_kv=1).

title: server: prompt cache is populated by rerank tasks that can never read it back (cache_idle_slots missing the SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION guard)
body:
### Summary

On a rerank-only server, host RAM grows by ~23 MB per `/v1/rerank` call until it reaches the `--cache-ram` limit (8192 MiB by default), and is never released while the process lives. The growth is the **prompt cache being populated by rerank tasks that can never read it back** - for `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_RERANK` the cache is write-only.

This is not the same as #25740 (closed as not-planned). There the cache was doing its job on the completion path and the reporter simply hadn't set `-cram 0`. Here the entries are provably never read, so the memory is pure waste plus a per-request serialisation cost.

### Version / environment

- `b4d6c7d8ff69c2e05e4e8ee7e6e710a08abd7b45` (b10091), also present on master at time of writing
- CUDA, aarch64 (NVIDIA GB10), driver 580.173.02
- Model: Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B Q8_0 GGUF
- Server: `llama-server --reranking --pooling rank -c 8192 -np 2 -ngl 999 -fa on --no-mmap`
- Reproduced identically on two hosts

### The path

1. `POST /v1/rerank` creates independent `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_RERANK` tasks with no parent.
2. `server_slot::release()` clears the prompt only for child tasks (`server-context.cpp:488-491`):
   ```cpp
   // do not keep context of the child slots - the parent's context is enough
   if (task->is_child()) {
       prompt_clear();
   }
   ```
   Rerank tasks are not children, so `slot.prompt` and its KV state survive release.
3. On the next task launch, the idle-slot pass saves every idle slot to the prompt cache (`server-context.cpp:2398-2414`) - **with no task-type guard**:
   ```cpp
   if (params_base.cache_idle_slots) {
       for (auto & slot : slots) {
           if (!slot.is_processing()) {
               if (slot.prompt_save(*prompt_cache)) {
   ```
4. The other call site does have the guard it needs (`server-context.cpp:1617-1618`):
   ```cpp
   // cache prompts only for completion tasks
   update_cache = update_cache && task.type == SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION;
   ```
5. `prompt_load` is only reached from inside that completion-gated branch, so nothing ever reads a rerank entry back.

With `-np 2`, `kv_unified` is false, so the `[TAG_IDLE_SLOT_CLEAR]` path does not run and the slot keeps its prompt after the save as well.

### Measurements

Fresh restart each arm, 40 calls, resident memory of the service:

| workload | growth |
|---|---|
| 40 calls, **identical** query+docs | +68 MB, then flat from call ~10 |
| 40 calls, 20 docs, **40 distinct** doc lengths | +3032 MB by call 20, climbing until capped |
| same, with `--cache-ram 0` | +626 MB |
| same, `--cache-ram 0` + `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | +620 MB (graph cache not involved) |
| same 40 lengths **descending** | +620 MB immediately, then flat |

Two separate effects: the cache (dominant, content-keyed, deduped only on full prefix match, so every distinct query+document pair is a new entry) and a benign high-water-mark buffer allocation of ~620 MB that stops growing once the largest request has been seen.

The arithmetic matches: Qwen3-0.6B is 28 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim, f16 → 112 KiB/token, so ~23 MB/call ≈ 210 tokens of KV state - a query plus a few short documents. In production the process sat at 9137 MB with **zero busy slots**, consistent with ~1.1 GB baseline plus the 8 GiB cap.

### Reproduce

```bash
llama-server -m Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf --reranking --pooling rank -c 8192 -np 2
# then POST /v1/rerank repeatedly with DIFFERENT documents each time and watch RSS.
# Identical documents will not reproduce it - the cache dedups on full prefix match.
```

### Suggested fix

Apply the same guard the completion path already uses, so idle slots are only saved for task types that can read the cache back:

```cpp
if (params_base.cache_idle_slots) {
    for (auto & slot : slots) {
        if (!slot.is_processing() && slot.task && slot.task->type == SERVER_TASK_TYPE_COMPLETION) {
```

Alternatively (or additionally) clear the prompt on release for task types that never reuse it.

### Workaround

`--cache-ram 0` (which also auto-disables `cache_idle_slots`), or `--no-cache-idle-slots`. For a rerank/embedding-only server this costs nothing, since those entries are never read. Confirmed: 9137 MB → ~1.1 GB steady state on our fleet.

### Note on scope

`/v1/embeddings` builds non-child `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_EMBEDDING` tasks through the same `send_embedding` → `release()` path, so it looks structurally exposed. I could **not** reproduce growth on an embedding-only server (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 30 distinct input lengths, +20 MB and flat), so I am reporting only what I measured rather than assuming.

- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

It would be very cool if llama.cpp SYCL used less VRAM

### Motivation

A while ago, the VRAM usage was more or less stable. Now, when you load a model, the VRAM used is different from when you send a prompt; when you send a prompt, the VRAM usage increases. This also happens when it enters the response phase. Right now the VRAM usage looks like: load=10000 -> prompt processing=11000 -> token generation=11050.

If SYCL used less VRAM, we would be able to allocate more layers to the GPU and also increase the batch sizes

Conversion to F16 completes successfully, writes 427 tensors across what the log reports as 32 transformer blocks (`blk.0`–`blk.31`).
2. Quantize to Q4_K_M with `llama-quantize` (same image) — completes successfully, all 427 tensors processed without error.

```
check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.32.attn_norm.weight' not found
llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
```

- Reproduced identically on two llama.cpp builds: `b10290` and a fresh self-built `b10360` (today's latest tag as of this report) — not a stale-build issue.
- The GGUF metadata includes `qwen35.nextn_predict_layers = 1` alongside the 32 regular transformer blocks. My guess (not verified against the source) is that the loader computes an expected layer count that includes this NextN/MTP layer (`n_layer + 1` → expects `blk.32`), while the converter only writes tensors for the 32 "real" transformer blocks — a mismatch between what the converter emits and what the loader expects for this specific architecture's NextN handling.

```

title: Eval bug: Metal: GGML_ASSERT(buf_src) failed in ggml_metal_buffer_set_tensor on Intel Mac with AMD discrete GPU (newBufferWithBytesNoCopy page-alignment requirement)
body:
### Name and Version

Built from source at tag b10358 (shallow clone, so the binary reports build: b1-030ebb5; commit 030ebb5). Also reproduced on b6440 (33daece86).

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Intel Xeon W (iMac Pro 2017, hw.model = iMacPro1,1) + AMD Radeon Pro Vega 56 (8 GB VRAM, discrete GPU over PCIe)

### Models

Qwen_Qwen3-8B-GGUF_Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce:

Build at tag b10358 on macOS Big Sur 11.7 with Apple clang 13 (CommandLineTools): cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON && cmake --build build --config Release
Run any GGUF with GPU offload enabled: ./build/bin/llama-cli -m model.gguf -ngl 1 -p "hello"
It aborts with GGML_ASSERT(buf_src) failed at ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.m:1862

Problem description

On an Intel Mac with a discrete AMD GPU, any run with GPU offload enabled aborts during the first decode with:

GGML_ASSERT(buf_src) failed at ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.m:1862

This happens with -ngl 1 as well as -ngl 999, so offloading a single tensor is enough to trigger it. The build itself succeeds (Apple clang 13 from CommandLineTools, cmake -DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON).

Call path: llama_decode → graph_compute → ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async → ggml_metal_buffer_set_tensor.

Root cause

In ggml_metal_buffer_set_tensor, the raw tensor pointer is handed to newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:

void * data_ptr = (void *)(uintptr_t) data;
id buf_src = [buf->dev->mtl_device newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:data_ptr length:size options:MTLResourceStorageModeShared deallocator:nil];
GGML_ASSERT(buf_src);
newBufferWithBytesNoCopy requires the pointer to be page-aligned (4096 bytes on Intel Macs) and returns nil otherwise. Tensor data loaded from a GGUF file is tightly packed, so this alignment is not guaranteed. buf_src becomes nil and the assert fires.

This path is only reached on non-unified-memory devices. The function starts with:

if (buf->is_shared) { memcpy((char *) tensor->data + offset, data, size); return; }
On Apple Silicon is_shared is true and the memcpy path returns early, so the newBufferWithBytesNoCopy path is never exercised there. That is consistent with the README listing Metal as an Apple Silicon backend, but the path is still compiled and taken on Intel + discrete AMD.

The same pattern exists in ggml_metal_buffer_get_tensor (line 1914), which passes the destination pointer directly. The other three uses of newBufferWithBytesNoCopy in this file (lines 1664, 1733, 1760) operate on already-aligned pointers and sizes and are fine.

Not a gpuAddress issue. MTLBuffer.gpuAddress is macOS 13.0+, and its absence does break builds on older SDKs, but that is a separate problem: the same assert is reported on macOS 13.7.8 (Intel iMac 2017 + Radeon Pro 580), where gpuAddress does exist.

GGML_METAL_CONCURRENCY_DISABLE=1 does not help. The variable is implemented (ggml-metal-context.m:137, res->use_concurrency = getenv("GGML_METAL_CONCURRENCY_DISABLE") == nil), but the abort occurs at the identical line with an identical stack.

Suggested fix

Allocate a buffer and copy into it, instead of wrapping an existing pointer. Cost is one memcpy.

set_tensor:

id buf_src = [buf->dev->mtl_device newBufferWithLength:size options:MTLResourceStorageModeShared];
GGML_ASSERT(buf_src);
memcpy([buf_src contents], data, size);
get_tensor:

id buf_dst = [buf->dev->mtl_device newBufferWithLength:size options:MTLResourceStorageModeShared];
GGML_ASSERT(buf_dst);
and, immediately AFTER [cmd_buf waitUntilCompleted]: memcpy(data, [buf_dst contents], size);
The ordering of the get_tensor memcpy matters: placing it before waitUntilCompleted reads the buffer before the blit completes, which does not crash but silently corrupts the data.

With these two changes the model loads and runs. Output is correct (prompt "hello" returns "Hello! How can I assist you today?"); I did not observe the output corruption reported for AMD discrete GPUs in #19563.

Secondary finding 1: most operations are not dispatched to Metal at all

has_simdgroup_reduction is set from two conditions only (ggml-metal-device.m:731-732):

supportsFamily:MTLGPUFamilyApple7
supportsFamily:MTLGPUFamilyMetal3_GGML, where MTLGPUFamilyMetal3_GGML is a hard-coded 5001 (line 26) because the constant is absent from the Big Sur SDK
Neither holds on Vega 56 under Big Sur, so has_simdgroup_reduction is false, and the twelve supports_op cases that return it (including GGML_OP_MUL_MAT) all return false. The scheduler consequently runs those ops on the CPU. The log confirms this directly:

resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device MTL0 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
So the backend loads, runs, and produces correct output on pre-Metal3 AMD hardware — it simply does almost no work on the GPU. This is a more precise statement than "the Metal backend does not work on pre-Metal3 AMD GPUs", which is the conclusion currently recorded in #15228.

Secondary finding 2: weights are not resident in VRAM

After the fix the load log reports the weights on the Metal side:

load_tensors: offloaded 37/37 layers to GPU
load_tensors: MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 4275.33 MiB
llama_kv_cache: MTL0_Private KV buffer size = 576.00 MiB
sched_reserve: MTL0_Private compute buffer size = 32.00 MiB
Monitoring VRAM with ioreg during inference:

idle: 712.2 MiB used
after model load: 1320.5 MiB used
during generation: 1321.4 MiB used, device utilization 10%, core clock 71 MHz, fan 0 RPM
The increase is 608.3 MiB, matching MTL0_Private KV (576.00) + compute (32.00) exactly. Nothing corresponding to the 4275.33 MiB of MTL0_Mapped weights is ever resident: the weights stay in host memory and are read over PCIe. This matches #15228.

Measured throughput on Qwen3 8B Q4_K_M is therefore not improved by offload: 17.4 t/s prompt with -ngl 999 -c 4096, against 53.4 t/s prompt / 12.9 t/s generation for CPU-only. -c 4096 is correctly applied (n_ctx = 4096 and KV 576.00 MiB confirmed in the log), and --no-repack makes it worse (14.7 t/s vs 17.4 t/s).

Diagnosability note

The device property block that logs GPU name, GPU family, simdgroup reduction, simdgroup matrix mul., has unified memory, has bfloat and has tensor (ggml-metal-device.m around line 936) never appears in any output on this configuration. It is missing from llama-cli with -v --log-file, from llama-cli captured through script, and from llama-server with -v, while the ggml_metal_init lines (allocating / found device / picking default device / use fusion / use concurrency / use graph optimize) are printed normally, twice. As a result a user cannot tell from the logs whether their GPU satisfies has_simdgroup_reduction. Making that block reliably visible would save a lot of guesswork on non-Apple-Silicon hardware.

Related issues

#15228 — weights mapped with Shared storage, read over PCIe on discrete GPUs (reopened 2026-02-19)
#19527 — PR addressing Metal performance on AMD discrete GPUs
#19563 — output corruption on AMD discrete GPUs
#25866 — GCN/Vega wave64 specific issue
I am happy to open a PR with the two-line fix if that is useful.



### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->
GGML_ASSERT(buf_src) failed at ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.m:1862

ggml_metal_init: found device: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 56 ggml_metal_init: picking default device: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 56

resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device MTL0 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support) resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled

load_tensors: offloaded 37/37 layers to GPU load_tensors: MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 4275.33 MiB llama_kv_cache: MTL0_Private KV buffer size = 576.00 MiB sched_reserve: MTL0_Private compute buffer size = 32.00 MiB
</details>

title: Eval bug: DeepSeek V4 Flash tokenizer blows its stack on long tool output
body:
### Name and Version

version: 10293 (a1f96d4fc)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97,887 MiB VRAM

### Models

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, UD-IQ1_S

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/1290dcca3f84612f646fb546fb9e8433c1b339b0/UD-IQ1_S

### Problem description & steps to reproduce


Hit this while running DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 through `llama-server`.

A large tool result containing one long run of ASCII letters crashes the server during tokenization, before inference gets a turn.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out llama.cpp commit `a1f96d4fc2c9e4101a6666a9d87f547e7e880df6`.

2. Build with CUDA and start the server:

```console
llama-server \
  -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ1_S-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  -c 16384 \
  -b 2048 \
  -ub 512 \
  -np 1 \
  --swa-full \
  -fa on \
  -ctk f16 \
  -ctv f16 \
  -ngl 999 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18082 \
  --jinja \
  --reasoning-format deepseek \
  --reasoning on \
  --reasoning-budget -1
```

3. Run an OpenAI-compatible tool-use conversation against `/v1/chat/completions`.

4. Have one tool produce a long letter run:

```console
python3 -c "print('Z' * 131072)"
```

5. Send the tool result back to the model. In the tested run, Pi 0.84.0 clipped it to 51,294 bytes.

Server falls over with `SIGSEGV` while tokenizing that request.

### What should happen

If the request is too large, return a normal context limit error and keep the server alive.

### What actually happens

libstdc++ piles up roughly 76,000 recursive `std::regex` frames and exhausts the worker thread stack. Backtrace ends up here:

```text
std::__detail::__regex_algo_impl
unicode_regex_split
llm_tokenizer_bpe_session::tokenize
llama_vocab::tokenize
common_tokenize
tokenize_input_prompts
server_routes::handle_completions_impl
```

GGUF has `tokenizer.ggml.pre` set to `joyai-llm`. That is just the pre-tokenizer compatibility tag. Its regex is also used by DeepSeek V3 and Hunyuan Dense.

No custom splitter handles this exact regex, so `unicode_regex_split()` punts it to `std::regex`. Long letter runs then chew through the thread stack.

A non-recursive splitter fixes the crash. Replaying the original request returns the expected `27940 tokens exceeds 16384 tokens` error, and `/health` stays `ok`.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

```console
  CUDA Version 12.8.1

  Thread 26 "llama-server" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
  [Switching to Thread 0x7ffd557f2000 (LWP 155)]

  #0      std::__detail::_Executor<...>::_M_dfs(...)
  #1      std::__detail::_Executor<...>::_M_rep_once_more(...)
          ... same two std::regex frames repeat about 76,000 times ...
  #76664  std::__detail::__regex_algo_impl(...)
  #76665  unicode_regex_split(...)
  #76666  llm_tokenizer_bpe_session::tokenize(...)
  #76667  llama_vocab::impl::tokenize(...)
  #76668  llama_vocab::tokenize(...)
  #76669  llama_vocab::tokenize(...)
  #76670  common_tokenize(...)
  #76671  tokenize_mixed(...)
  #76672  tokenize_input_subprompt(...)
  #76673  tokenize_input_prompts(...)
  #76674  server_routes::handle_completions_impl(...)
```

Full backtrace contains 76,685 frames. Almost all intermediate frames alternate between `std::__detail::_Executor::_M_dfs()` and `_M_rep_once_more()`.

The crash happens while tokenizing the request, before prompt evaluation starts.

</details>

title: DFlash: corrupted predicted_ms on some Q4/Metal requests
body:
## DFlash `predicted_ms` becomes impossible on some Q4/Metal requests

On the current upstream commit `9ba73fd1f5bc882d4cb58101a99e99f4f326506c`, I see corrupted server decode timing fields for DFlash on Apple Metal.

Configuration:

- MacBook Air M4, 24 GB unified memory; Metal build.
- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` converted to `Q4_K_M`.
- Draft: `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` converted to BF16 GGUF.
- `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 --temp 0 --top-k 1 -np 1 -c 4096 --jinja --metrics`.
- No-thinking greedy requests (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`).

In a 33-sample / 39-turn SPEED-Bench qualitative run, all requests returned HTTP 200. For three math requests, client wall-clock latency was about 36 seconds with a 256-token completion, but the response timing fields were implausibly large:

| question ID | client latency | completion tokens | `timings.predicted_ms` | reported `predicted_per_second` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `47534ec0377943708c55cb1bfad6c83d` | 35.707 s | 256 | 2,198,466.543 ms | 0.1164 tok/s |
| `f73440d5701f4feeaeffcacf282d5607` | 35.832 s | 256 | 206,481.456 ms | 1.2398 tok/s |
| `10983429e00549a3bf63b7ea733195af` | 37.950 s | 256 | 2,675,502.216 ms | 0.0957 tok/s |

The same prompt IDs under the no-speculation Q4 baseline reported 19.9–22.3 s client latency and 19,813–22,259 ms `predicted_ms`, which is internally consistent. Other DFlash requests in the same run also had `predicted_ms` close to client elapsed time.

title: Misc. bug: GGUF loader accepts a tensor size that wraps to 0 after padding
body:
### Name and Version

$ bin/llama-gguf --version
(inspection tool built from this repo; same ggml/gguf code path as llama-cli)

Tested commit: master 9558fa44 (also confirmed on branch gguf-pad-wrap-guard
with the fix). Debug build, AppleClang, Darwin arm64. The vulnerable code is
in ggml/src/gguf.cpp (gguf_init_from_reader) and is not tied to this commit;
it has been present for a long time.

### Operating systems

Mac, Other? (Please let us know in description)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library), Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell
# build the example tool
cmake -S . -B build -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build --target llama-gguf

# trigger: read a crafted GGUF with tensor-data checking enabled
bin/llama-gguf poc/pad_wrap.gguf r

# PoC generator (poc/gen_pad_wrap.py) builds poc/pad_wrap.gguf (384 bytes):
#   tensor a: F32, 64 elts, 256 bytes (valid)
#   tensor b: F32, ne = [4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1]
#            ggml_nbytes = 4 * 4 * (2^30 - 1) * (2^30 + 1) = 2^64 - 16
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

gguf_init_from_reader accumulates each tensor's padded size into ctx->size:

    size_t padded_size = GGML_PAD(ggml_nbytes(&ti.t), ctx->alignment);
    if (SIZE_MAX - ctx->size < padded_size) { /* reject */ }
    ctx->size += padded_size;

GGML_PAD rounds up: GGML_PAD(x, n) = ((x) + (n) - 1) & ~((n) - 1).
When ggml_nbytes is within (alignment - 1) of SIZE_MAX, the (x) + (n - 1)
addition wraps to a small value and the mask clears it to 0. With the default
alignment (32) and nbytes = 2^64 - 16:

    GGML_PAD(2^64 - 16, 32)
      = ((2^64 - 16) + 31) & ~31
      = (15) & ~31          // 64-bit overflow on the add
      = 0

So padded_size becomes 0, the SIZE_MAX guard (which checks padded_size, not
nbytes) always passes, and ctx->size only records tensor a's 256 bytes.
Tensor b still gets a ggml_tensor with ne = [4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1]
and a data pointer at the end of the 256-byte backing blob, but the context
no longer reflects its real size.

Downstream code that trusts the context size, or iterates a tensor by its
own dimensions, then reads out of bounds. examples/gguf hits this directly
(see logs): it accepts size = 18446744073709551600, reads b's data past the
backing blob, and aborts.

The wrap lands on exactly 0 for every power-of-two alignment (checked over
all 32 possible alignment values), so the window is reliably hit, not a
near-miss.

Suggested fix: reject before padding when nbytes + (alignment - 1) would
overflow. ctx->alignment is already validated as a non-zero power of two
earlier in the same function, so (alignment - 1) cannot underflow.

    const size_t nbytes = ggml_nbytes(&ti.t);
    if (nbytes > SIZE_MAX - (ctx->alignment - 1)) {
        GGML_LOG_ERROR("%s: tensor '%s' size %zu overflows after padding (alignment %zu)\n",
            __func__, ti.t.name, nbytes, ctx->alignment);
        gguf_free(ctx);
        return nullptr;
    }
    const size_t padded_size = GGML_PAD(nbytes, ctx->alignment);
    if (SIZE_MAX - ctx->size < padded_size) { /* reject */ }
    ctx->size += padded_size;

A test-gguf handcrafted case (TENSORS_NBYTES_PAD_WRAP, single F32 tensor with
the same ne) flips with this fix: master accepts (returns non-null), patched
rejects (returns null).

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression. The GGML_PAD-based accumulation in gguf_init_from_reader
has been there for a long time; no single commit introduced it.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

master 9558fa44 (bin/llama-gguf poc/pad_wrap.gguf r) -- accepts the wrapped
size, reads tensor b out of bounds, aborts:

```console
gguf_ex_read_1: tensor[1]: name = b, size = 18446744073709551600, offset = 256, type = f32, n_elts = 4611686018427387900
gguf_ex_read_1: reading tensor 1 data
gguf_ex_read_1: tensor[1]: n_dims = 3, ne = (4, 1073741823, 1073741825, 1), name = b, data = 0x104c90270
b data[:10] : 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000
examples/gguf/gguf.cpp:269: GGML_ASSERT(gguf_ex_read_1(fname, check_data) && "failed to read gguf file") failed
```

b's data pointer (0x...270) is 256 bytes past a's (0x...170), i.e. one byte
after the 256-byte backing blob. data[0] reads out of bounds and returns
0.0; the check_data loop then aborts on the value mismatch. Exit 134.

Note: ASAN does not flag this over-read. ggml sub-allocates each tensor from
a larger arena, so the few bytes read past b stay inside one malloc region.
The assert message is the proof the read left b's own data. A harness that
walks b's full declared extent SEGVs about 15.7 KB past the arena.

With the fix (branch gguf-pad-wrap-guard), the same command rejects at the
parser before any tensor data is built:

```console
gguf_init_from_reader: tensor 'b' size 18446744073709551600 overflows after padding (alignment 32)
gguf_ex_read_0: failed to load 'poc/pad_wrap.gguf'
```

examples/gguf-hash on the same PoC: --xxh64 returns a bogus hash silently
(the 2^64 - 16 length wraps the internal input+len pointer, main loop is
skipped); --all (sha1/sha256) hangs walking the declared extent.

</details>

title: Eval bug: gemma4uv mmproj + CUDA → SIGABRT in mtmd_helper_decode_image_chunk → llama_context::decode (workarounds from #24251 and #24314 do not help)
body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10375 (533fa7f9)
built with ... for Linux x86_64 (CUDA build, RTX 4090)
```

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS container, kernel 6.12)

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- CPU: AMD EPYC 7502 x128
- RAM: 1 TiB system
- GPU: 1 x NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GiB VRAM, driver 580.x, CUDA 12.x)
- 32 GiB free VRAM at the moment of the crash

### Models

- Text: `Gemma4-31B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced-Q4_K_M.gguf` (18.7 GB)
- Vision: `mmproj-Gemma4-31B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced-BF16.gguf` (1.2 GB)
- Draft MTP: `mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf` (280 MB) — **NOT loaded in this repro; the bug reproduces with MTP disabled.**

### Problem description

Loading any image via the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint
crashes the server with SIGABRT, even after applying the workarounds
recommended in issues #24251 and #24314.

Reproduction:

```bash
llama-server \
  --model /root/rivermind-data/llm-models/hauhaucs-gemma4-31b-qat-uncensored-mtp/Gemma4-31B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj /root/rivermind-data/llm-models/hauhaucs-gemma4-31b-qat-uncensored-mtp/mmproj-Gemma4-31B-QAT-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Balanced-BF16.gguf \
  --no-mmproj-offload \
  --no-warmup \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8081 --api-key *** \
  --ctx-size 8192 --parallel 1 --cont-batching --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 128 \
  -ngl 99 -fa on \
  --temp 0.6 --top-k 64 --top-p 0.9 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.1 \
  --no-webui --jinja --log-timestamps
```

(The same crash reproduces with `--spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft <mtp.gguf>`
added; MTP draft is orthogonal to this crash.)

Send a request with even a trivial 1x1 PNG image:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"hauhau-gemma4-31b-uncensored-mtp","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[
    {"type":"text","text":"What color? one word."},
    {"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."}}
  ]}],"max_tokens":30}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/chat/completions
```

The server processes the first request OK and returns a response — but on a
*subsequent* image request, the process aborts. (If the first request itself
succeeds and only later requests fail, that's the failure mode I observed
twice in this session. The crash may also occur on the very first request if
the upstream is load-balancing; I have not narrowed this down further.)

### Stack trace

```
ggml_print_backtrace () from /opt/llama.cpp/b10375/build/bin/libggml-base.so.0
ggml_abort () from /opt/llama.cpp/b10375/build/bin/libggml-base.so.0
llama_context::decode(llama_batch const&) () from .../libllama.so.0
llama_decode () from .../libllama.so.0
mtmd_helper_decode_image_chunk () from .../libmtmd.so.0
server_slot::process_mtmd_chunk(unsigned long, unsigned long&)
server_context_impl::pre_decode()::{lambda(server_slot&)#5}::operator()(server_slot&)
server_context_impl::iterate(...)
server_context_impl::pre_decode()
server_context_impl::update_slots()
server_queue::start_loop(long)
```

### What I tried (and that did NOT help)

| Workaround | Source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--no-mmproj-offload` (run vision encoder on CPU) | issue #24251 | Still crashes; same stack |
| Drop MTP draft (`--spec-type draft-mtp` removed) | issue #24314 | Still crashes; same stack |
| Combined both workarounds | this report | Still crashes; same stack |
| Smaller batch/ubatch (`-b 128 -ub 32`) | — | Still crashes; same stack |
| Disable flash attention (`-fa off`) | — | Crashes; same stack |
| `--parallel 1` (default already) | — | Crashes; same stack |
| 1x1 PNG input (simplest possible image) | — | Crashes; same stack |

The crash is NOT memory-related: GPU was 20 GiB / 24 GiB used, well within
limits. The crash is NOT MTP-related: reproduces with no draft model loaded.

### Workaround that DOES work

Drop `--mmproj` entirely. Vision is unavailable, but the text-only server is
stable. This is the only config I can run in production on this build.

### Expected Behavior

Loading Gemma 4 with its bundled `mmproj-...BF16.gguf` and sending an image
should produce a coherent response, with the vision encoder running on CPU
if that is the safer path for this architecture.

### Actual Behavior

SIGABRT in `mtmd_helper_decode_image_chunk → llama_context::decode`. Process
exits, GPU memory released, server stops listening on the port. Any pending
or subsequent requests (text or image) get connection refused.

### Relation to other issues

- #24251 (gemma4uv on GPU → NaN logits → sampler assert): different stack
  (sampler, not decode). Possibly a separate manifestation of the same root
  cause.
- #24314 (MTP + mmproj + flash-attn → memory aperture violation on
  Ada/Blackwell): different stack (fattn.cu, not llama_decode). Triggered by
  MTP draft; mine reproduces with MTP disabled.
- #25522 (Gemma 4 crashes with MTP): depends on MTP draft.
- #24324 (llama.cpp-b9568 fattn.cu:579): also depends on MTP draft.

So this is a fourth Gemma 4 vision crash path. They may share an upstream
cause — the gemma4uv vision encoder interacting poorly with CUDA graphs on
Ada/Blackwell — but I have not bisected.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. I only have b10375 to test on this machine. Issues #24251,
#24314, #25522 are all on builds ≤ b10375; issue #21402 cites b8639, b8650
already showing a similar load-time abort. The bug has been present for a
while.

### Hardware

```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version,compute_cap --format=csv
name, memory.total [MiB], driver_version, compute_cap
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24564 MiB, 580.65.06, 8.9
```

Compute capability 8.9 (sm_89, Ada Lovelace). The patterns reported in
#24314 (memory aperture violation) and #24251 (NaN logits on GPU) suggest
this generation is particularly affected.

title: HIP backend silently corrupts Qwen3.5-27B (Gated DeltaNet) inference on gfx1151 - oldest context lost; Vulkan correct at identical commit
body:
### Summary

On **gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Windows 11)** the **HIP backend silently corrupts inference of Qwen3.5-27B** (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet architecture, tested as VLM with mmproj): the **oldest part of the context is consistently lost** while output stays fluent and deterministic. The **Vulkan backend at the identical commit is correct**. We ran an extensive exclusion campaign (details below); every individually testable component passes, so the defect appears to live at graph-composition level of the GDN block on HIP.

### Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU (**gfx1151**), 128 GB unified memory
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 26200, Adrenalin driver 32.0.31035.1003
- ROCm runtime: TheRock `therock-dist-windows-gfx1151-7.14.0rc3` (also reproduced with a different ROCm 7.x runtime DLL set)
- llama.cpp: official release zips `llama-b10453-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip` **and** `llama-b10582-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64.zip`, **and** a self-built b10582 (e85caa81e) with the TheRock clang toolchain — **all three affected identically**
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (unsloth GGUF) + mmproj BF16
- Counter-checks: **Vulkan builds of the very same commits (b10453 and b10582) are correct**; Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (pure attention, no GDN) is correct on the same HIP builds

### Reproduction (deterministic, temp 0)

Generate a synthetic 4-panel test image (no external assets needed):

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
W,H=660,640; img=Image.new('RGB',(W,H),'white'); d=ImageDraw.Draw(img)
try: fb=ImageFont.truetype('arialbd.ttf',20); fs=ImageFont.truetype('arial.ttf',14)
except: fb=fs=ImageFont.load_default()
for x,y,t,c in [(0,0,'Alpha Risk','Risk from parallel shifts of the reference rate.'),
                (330,0,'Beta Risk','Risk from non-parallel curve changes.'),
                (0,320,'Gamma Risk','Risk from embedded options, e.g. early repayment.'),
                (330,320,'Delta Risk','Risk from hedging with different rate indices.')]:
    d.rectangle([x+2,y+2,x+328,y+318],outline='black',width=2)
    d.ellipse([x+12,y+16,x+22,y+26],fill='black'); d.text((x+30,y+12),t,fill='black',font=fb)
    d.rectangle([x+30,y+50,x+290,y+200],outline='gray')
    if 'Gamma' in t:
        for i,bh in enumerate([60,90,130,100,80]): d.rectangle([x+50+i*45,y+195-bh,x+80+i*45,y+195],fill='gray')
    else: d.line([(x+40+i*25,y+190-int(12*(i**1.2))) for i in range(10)],fill='black',width=2)
    d.text((x+30,y+215),c,fill='black',font=fs)
img.save('synthetic_4panel.png')
```

```
llama-mtmd-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-BF16.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 4096 --temp 0 --seed 42 --image synthetic_4panel.png \
  -p "List ALL bold bullet headings in this image, top-left to bottom-right. Only the list."
```

- **HIP (gfx1151):** `['Beta Risk', 'Gamma Risk', 'Delta Risk']` — **top-left "Alpha Risk" (the oldest image tokens in raster order) is dropped**
- **Vulkan (same commit, same machine):** all four headings
- With a denser real-world 4-panel document scan the effect is stronger: HIP loses the entire upper half (0/4 headings) while Vulkan stays 4/4; flipping the image vertically "heals" it (the previously-top content becomes the newest tokens), which points at recency-position rather than image-coordinates.

### Exclusion campaign (everything below was tested on the same machine)

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime-DLL mismatch | official b10453 binary + clean matching TheRock 7.14 runtime | still wrong |
| Code regression / fix between builds | b10453 **and** b10582 built for **Vulkan** (same commits) | both correct → code exonerated |
| Toolchain | self-built HIP b10582 (TheRock clang) | reproduces official zips exactly |
| mtmd preprocessing | top-half crop alone is read fine; full preprocessing chain reviewed | exonerated |
| hipGraphs | `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` | still wrong |
| ubatch state handoff | `-ub 128 / 512 / 8192` (whole prompt in one ubatch) | still wrong |
| GATED_DELTA_NET kernel | `test-backend-ops -o GATED_DELTA_NET`, **including added prefill-scale cases** (n_seq_tokens 64/256/1024 at the real 32x128 geometry, v_repeat 2, and K=4/8 snapshot slots — upstream currently tests max n_seq_tokens=4 and K>1 only with tiny shapes) | **43/43 pass at NMSE 1e-7** |
| Any other op in the graph | per-op sweep: SSM_CONV, CUMSUM, L2_NORM, RMS_NORM, EXP, SIGMOID, SOFT_MAX, ADD, MUL, SCALE, CPY, SET_ROWS, GET_ROWS, ROPE, FLASH_ATTN_EXT, GLU, SUM_ROWS, TRI, MUL_MAT_ID, MUL_MAT (>6400 cases total) | all pass |

Test-case additions we used (happy to open a PR):

```diff
     test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 64, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1, 2));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 256, 1, 1, false, false, 4));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1, 1, false, false, 4));
+    test_cases.emplace_back(new test_gated_delta_net(GGML_TYPE_F32, 32, 128, 1024, 1, 2, false, false, 8));
```

### Possibly related observations (same machine, can file separately)

1. `test-backend-ops -o SOLVE_TRI` crashes on this HIP setup with `rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidImage'` / "device kernel image is invalid" after 6 passing cases — this also makes the **unfused** gated-delta-net graph path unusable on HIP, so we could not A/B fused vs. unfused. (Filed separately.)
2. `llama-mtmd-cli` dies silently (no error output after "llama threadpool init") whenever CPU layers participate (`-ngl < 99` and `-ngl 0`), on our HIP **and** Vulkan self-builds — this blocked partial-offload bisection.

### Ask

Since every op passes in isolation at 1e-7 but the composed model degrades deterministically (and only on HIP), we suspect the HIP-specific composition of the GDN block (fused-graph variant selection, recurrent-state handling, or an interaction invisible to single-op tests). Happy to run any diagnostics/patches on this hardware — the repro is fully deterministic and takes ~40 s per run.
